projects.title: Measuring Entrepreneurial and Industry Identity in the Asteroid-Mining Industry with NLP
projects.summary: Analyse how entrepreneurs and institutions describe themselves as the asteroid-mining industry takes shape. The student builds an NLP pipeline that collects longitudinal text data (including Internet Archive company websites, communications, interviews and media) and a machine learning model separating general topics, individual identity claims and collective industry claims, validated against a manually annotated sample.

projects.title: Tracking Novel Research Through the Publication Process: A Text-Embedding Approach
projects.summary: Study scientific conservatism in peer review by measuring the novelty of submitted manuscripts with text embedding models. The student reviews embedding models for semantic similarity and builds a framework matching rejected papers to their eventual publications, using anonymized manuscript and peer review data from more than 2,000 Elsevier journals via the ICSR Lab.

projects.title: Active Sound Source Localization and Ego-Noise Mitigation for Mobile Robots
projects.summary: Develop an onboard acoustic localization framework in which a mobile robot with a microphone array suppresses its own ego-noise and localizes sound sources with multi-channel methods such as GCC-PHAT, SRP-PHAT or trilateration. The solution is deployed and evaluated on real robot hardware.

projects.title: Asymmetric Multi-modal Deep Vision Model Compression
projects.summary: Reduce the memory footprint, inference time and energy cost of RGB-thermal deep vision networks for deployment on small robots with limited compute, using techniques such as pruning and quantization. The project also studies how different visual modalities respond to compression.

projects.title: Comparing PSO and Reinforcement Learning for Training Robot Controllers
projects.summary: Fairly compare Particle Swarm Optimization and reinforcement learning when both train the same feedforward neural network controller on a multi-robot benchmark. The project includes a literature review, implementation of both algorithms in a high-fidelity simulator, and an analysis of the solutions found under comparable evaluation budgets.

projects.title: Cooperative Gas Source Localization with Infrastructure-Free UWB Positioning
projects.summary: Investigate cooperative gas source localization with heterogeneous robot teams whose positions come from infrastructure-free UWB relative localization. The student builds a simplified 2D gas-source environment, implements a cooperative estimation algorithm, and evaluates it with ground-truth, noisy and UWB-estimated robot positions.

projects.title: Multi-Robot Inspection with ToF-Based Replanning
projects.summary: Detect, cell by cell, where an inspected asset differs from its prior voxel map using onboard Time-of-Flight depth frames, and replan viewpoints and task assignments accordingly. The detection runs onboard and is evaluated in Webots on modified assets, with real MAVs if time allows.

projects.title: Reinforcement Learning for Gas Source Localization
projects.summary: Project on using reinforcement learning to localize gas sources (DISAL-MP60).

projects.title: Robotic Gas Sensor Calibration
projects.summary: Design an efficient pre-flight calibration set-up for low-cost MOX and PID gas sensors on a quadcopter, integrating temperature, humidity, flow, gas sensors, pump, valve and quadcopter. The goal is to estimate absolute gas concentration and compensate slow sensor dynamics.

projects.title: Robust indoor–outdoor state estimation for a compact multirotor
projects.summary: Measure and model how visual-inertial odometry and GNSS degrade during outdoor-to-indoor and indoor-to-outdoor transitions on compact MAVs, then design and test a fusion strategy that keeps position estimates continuous through a doorway. A master project may also study AprilTag fiducial markers as absolute position anchors.

projects.title: Thermal Burst Imaging for Optical Gas Imaging
projects.summary: Increase the signal of thermal camera frames for weak gas-leak detection by burst imaging, using dense image matching that is robust to camera motion and dynamic scenes. The project can use classic variational methods, learned methods, or a combination.

projects.title: Three-Dimensional UWB Localization for Heterogeneous Ground–Aerial Robot Teams
projects.summary: Extend an existing Webots UWB localization simulation so that aerial robots can act as mobile tags, adapting estimation algorithms to 3D positioning with realistic LOS/NLOS measurement models. The work is evaluated across environments, anchor configurations and aerial trajectories, with optional hardware-in-the-loop and motion-capture experiments for a master project.

projects.title: Vision-Language Uncertainty Maps for Drone Search
projects.summary: Build a per-cell probability and uncertainty map of target locations for drone search by combining a satellite-image prior scored against an operator's text description with in-flight drone image evidence from a fine-tuned compact vision-language model. The method is benchmarked in simulation on satellite images with known target locations, with optional operator clarification requests.

projects.title: 3D Computer Vision for Underwater Videos of Reefs
projects.summary: Project applying 3D computer vision to underwater videos of coral reefs.

projects.title: AI for topographic mapping
projects.summary: Develop new AI models that are robust and effective in real-world scenarios for land cover and land use mapping from satellite and aerial imagery. The work targets three challenges: hard-to-delimit class boundaries, incorporating multi-modal data such as text and ground-level images, and model interpretability.

projects.title: An AI assistant to interact with remote sensing images
projects.summary: Develop a natural-language interface that lets non-expert users ask questions in English about satellite images and receive answers in English. The work targets remote sensing visual question answering and aims to make the reasoning behind answers transparent and interpretable. The project is carried out with the Φ-lab at the European Space Agency and the Université de Paris Cité.

projects.title: Integrating phylogeny into species distribution models
projects.summary: Project on integrating phylogenetic information into species distribution models.

projects.title: KG4GEO: A Knowledge Graph for the World Geography
projects.summary: Project on building a knowledge graph of world geography.

projects.title: Knowledge-guided Explanations for Satellite Images
projects.summary: The project aims to develop approaches that describe satellite images and their changes in natural language, producing explanations accessible to non-experts. It combines machine learning for Earth observation with knowledge from large textual corpora such as Wikipedia and specialized web pages, in collaboration with the NLP lab.

projects.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Satellite Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
projects.summary: Project on self-supervised learning from satellite images using a joint-embedding predictive architecture.

projects.title: Self-supervised pretraining for deforestation drivers classification
projects.summary: Project on self-supervised pretraining for classifying the drivers of deforestation.

projects.title: Species distribution modelling with multi-modal deep learning
projects.summary: Project on species distribution modelling using multi-modal deep learning.

projects.title: Transforming Underwriting for Commercial Insurance with High-Resolution Remote Sensing
projects.summary: The project addresses the issue of limited labeled data in very high resolution aerial imagery. It aims to learn change-detection models efficiently in this setting. The project is a partnership with AXA.

projects.title: Accurate Simulation of Materials with Graph Neural Network Finite Element Models
projects.summary: The student will incorporate material constitutive laws into a graph neural network so that it predicts material stress accurately, instead of relying only on the parameters tracked in the dataset. The project evaluates this physics-informed approach against learning stress as a distinct objective.

projects.title: Battery Lifetime Prediction under Changing Operating Conditions with Neural SDEs
projects.summary: This semester project develops Neural Stochastic Differential Equations to model battery degradation and predict capacity and remaining useful life under changing future operating conditions. The student will use NASA's ProgPy battery simulator and evaluate on unseen operating schedules.

projects.title: Building Self-Improving AI Research Agents for Prognostics and Health Management
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a self-improving agentic AI system that extracts structured knowledge from prognostics and health management research papers and links it to benchmark tasks and evaluation criteria. The expected outcome is a prototype literature-to-evaluation pipeline for PHM research agents.

projects.title: Data-Driven Prioritization of Railway Track Inspections
projects.summary: This semester project uses historical SBB track measurements, infrastructure data and maintenance records to test whether data-driven methods can identify track sections likely to need maintenance. The goal is to design predictive models and prioritization strategies for railway inspection within a limited inspection budget.

projects.title: Federated Foundation Models for Electricity Load Forecasting
projects.summary: The project explores federated adaptation of time-series foundation models, using parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA, for electricity load forecasting on smart-meter data. The student will build a federated fine-tuning pipeline and benchmark it against zero-shot, local fine-tuning and centralised training.

projects.title: Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for Composite Material Simulation
projects.summary: The student will add physics and engineering inductive bias to a state-of-the-art graph neural network surrogate for finite element simulations, to improve performance and stability. The goal is to evaluate stable rollouts and simulate dynamic oscillations of simple structures such as composite plates.

projects.title: Robust Multi-Modal 3D Reconstruction
projects.summary: The project aims to make 3D scene reconstruction (NeRF and Gaussian Splatting) robust to missing pixel-level alignment between RGB and other modalities, with a focus on RGB and thermal imaging. The student will investigate contrastive learning for cross-modal correspondences and 3D feature alignment.

projects.title: Structure-Aware Generative Models for Spatiotemporal Systems
projects.summary: The student will explore how to incorporate structural information into generative models such as diffusion and flow matching models to learn the dynamics of sensor networks in industrial systems. The goal is to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of these models for spatiotemporal signal processing.

projects.title: Test-time Domain Adaptation for OOD Detection
projects.summary: The student will work on out-of-distribution detection under domain shift by applying test-time domain adaptation online during inference. The goal is to explore existing test-time adaptation methods and improve and modify them for OOD detection.

projects.title: How Was the Climate of the French Colonies Taught? A Study of Geography Textbooks from the Late 19th Century to the Mid-20th Century
projects.summary: Use text mining on dozens of French geography textbooks from Gallica to study how the climate and meteorology of the French colonies were taught in schools between the late Second Empire and the Third Republic, and whether a hierarchy among colonial climates existed in these representations.

projects.title: Mapping Open Science Platform
projects.summary: Crawl the web to identify links between open science platforms (repositories, journals, directories, search engines), characterise the nature of these links, and generate an interactive map of the open science network.

projects.title: The ecology of eucalyptus: Tracing the acclimatization and exploitation of eucalyptus in Europe through 19th-century French publications
projects.summary: Use text mining on about 3,660 19th-century French books mentioning eucalyptus, harvested from Gallica, to study how publications on the tree evolved and which properties (medicinal, forestry, agricultural) were associated with it. Possible methods include co-occurrence networks, topic modelling, sentiment analysis and named entity recognition.

projects.title: The 'ecosystem' of open science: Tracing the Evolution of Ecological Metaphors in Discourses on the Digital Transition of Research
projects.summary: Assemble a heterogeneous corpus of scientific, policy and oral texts on the digital transition of research, then trace the emergence and circulation of ecological metaphors either with NLP-based automated literature review or with a multi-layered diachronic network analysis.

projects.title: The Global Footprint of the Swiss Economy and Society: A Data-Driven Analysis of Trading Patterns in the 20th Century
projects.summary: Build a pipeline to extract data from scanned Swiss trade statistics (1890-2000) and integrate it into a database, in order to support a long-term analysis of Switzerland's material and environmental footprint. The student may then examine a research question such as the evolution of the carbon footprint or of critical materials.

projects.title: The use of images in health textbooks: how images and scientific discourse on gender interact between 1870 and 1940
projects.summary: Extract and classify the illustrations in about eighty French-language health manuals (1870-1940) from digitized library collections, then analyse how depictions of men and women shape medical discourse on gender. The project is part of the SNSF-funded MEDIF project and is carried out with the Institut des humanités en médecine (IHM).

projects.title: Accelerating geophysical flow simulation using machine learning
projects.summary: Develop machine learning surrogate models, purely data-driven or physics-informed, that approximate high-fidelity physics-based geophysical flow simulations (e.g., MPM or DEM on 3D terrains) at a much lower computational cost. The surrogate is to be evaluated on velocity fields, runout distances and deposition patterns on unseen terrains. The project is supervised jointly with the Chair of Alpine Mass Movements at ETH Zurich.

projects.title: AI-Enhanced Characterization of Internal Material Properties from Surface Observations
projects.summary: Develop a generalized inverse modeling framework that uses deep learning to infer internal material property distributions from observable surface responses such as displacement fields. The approach uses high-fidelity simulations, robust feature extraction and regularization to handle the ill-posedness of the inverse problem.

projects.title: Digital twin simulation of rockfall hazards
projects.summary: Develop a digital twin framework for simulating and assessing rockfall hazards in real-world terrains, using terrain reconstruction and the lab's in-house DEM code to model rockfall trajectories and barrier interactions. The project also explores uncertainty quantification and machine learning surrogate models for risk mapping.

projects.title: Experimental Investigation of Architected Granular Materials
projects.summary: The project studies architected granular materials, where particle shape, surface properties and packing are designed to control macroscopic mechanical behavior. Students will 3D-print custom particles, assemble granular packings, run static and dynamic mechanical tests with digital image correlation and imaging, and link microscale interactions to macroscale stiffness and energy absorption.

projects.title: Frictional instabilities in topologically interlocked structures
projects.summary: The project studies how stick-slip frictional instabilities and interfacial heterogeneity affect the failure of topologically interlocked structures. The student will use the level-set discrete element modeling framework to investigate their dynamic behavior under various conditions.

projects.title: Graph Neural Networks for Granular Mechanics
projects.summary: The project uses Graph Neural Networks to study how force-chain networks in granular materials evolve under shear, focusing on the approach to unjamming and failure. Models are to be trained on discrete element simulations and grain-scale experimental measurements.

projects.title: Multiphysics modeling of fault gouge
projects.summary: The student will combine discrete and continuum simulations to study fault gouge rheology, focusing on material heterogeneity, grain-scale characteristics such as particle fracture, and hydromechanical and thermomechanical coupling. The goal is to gain insight into earthquake mechanics.

projects.title: Phase-field modeling of fracture in architected structural materials
projects.summary: The project aims to develop and apply phase-field fracture models to simulate crack initiation and propagation in architected materials such as truss lattices and bioinspired composites. The goal is to understand how microstructural features (periodicity, hierarchy, intentional defects) affect fracture toughness, fracture modes and energy dissipation, with an option to explore machine-learning surrogate models for phase-field evolution.

projects.title: Physics-informed Deep Neural Operators for Solid Mechanics
projects.summary: The student explores the application of physics-informed deep neural operators (PINOs) to solid mechanics problems, simulating material behavior under various loading conditions in geotechnical or structural engineering contexts. The generalization ability of the method is evaluated and its accuracy is compared with conventional numerical solutions.

projects.title: Segregation in Granular Flows
projects.summary: Numerical study of how particle shape and size affect segregation of particles under shear and gravity-driven granular flow, by analysing the inter-particle forces. The goal is to inform continuum modelling of segregation in different scenarios.

projects.title: Automatic georeferencing of historical cadastres
projects.summary: Develop automatic computer vision and graph neural network methods to georeference the sheets of the Napoleonic and renovated European cadastres, enabling large-scale studies of territorial change over two centuries.

projects.title: Automatic transcription of Polier notebooks
projects.summary: Automatically transcribe the handwritten Polier notebooks (1754-1791, about 26,300 pages) using handwritten text recognition, then apply NLP-based distant reading to research economic, social or environmental history in Lausanne.

projects.title: Automatic vectorization of the renovated cadastre of Lausanne
projects.summary: Transform the 1888 renovated cadastre of Lausanne (over 300 plates) into vector maps using CNN-based semantic segmentation, and optionally use handwritten text recognition to process its legend of land uses and owners.

projects.title: Beyond Cheese and Chocolate: The Economic Landscape of Historical Switzerland
projects.summary: Realign the addresses of Swiss commercial registers (1883 onward) into geographic coordinates using modern geospatial references and historical place-name databases, to reconstruct the historical economic landscape of Switzerland and analyse it spatially.

projects.title: Cartonomics / Visual semiotics
projects.summary: Extract and analyse the visual symbols and representational elements of cartography across a large map corpus, studying how conventions for relief, elevation, buildings, water and natural landscape evolved over time, using deep learning and statistical methods.

projects.title: Door-to-door
projects.summary: Analyse a 10-year sample of 1880 Lausanne city directories extracted via OCR, then compare trades with Paris and New York datasets, to understand the specific commercial signature of each city. Datasets are to be published online.

projects.title: Enlumina
projects.summary: Index the visual elements of illuminated medieval manuscripts by segmenting and annotating depictions, training supervised and unsupervised (multimodal LLM) methods, and building a prototype search engine searchable by text and by visual similarity. The project also aims to study authorship attribution of copyists through visual similarity.

projects.title: European Postcards
projects.summary: Geolocate and reposition historical postcards of European places from Europeana using an AI-based semantic identifier and prompting, then publish them in the Time Machine Atlas interface. The project also involves working with the APIs of OpenAI and other AI providers.

projects.title: Haussmannian transformations in Paris during the XIXth century
projects.summary: Convert the 19th-century Paris maps of the Bibliothèque historique de la Ville de Paris from raster into vector geometry using CNN-based pixelwise classification and classic computer vision, then quantitatively analyse the transformation of the urban fabric.

projects.title: Icono Lausanne – Reorientation of the photographic archives of the Historical Museum
projects.summary: Develop automatic photogrammetry and neural network methods to match the roughly 38,500 digitised photographs of the Historical Museum of Lausanne and infer their camera angle and position, enabling reprojection of historical photographs onto 4D models.

projects.title: Lausanne 1722
projects.summary: Enrich the already georeferenced and vectorised Melotte cadastre of Lausanne (1721-1722) with socio-economic information on land use, function and ownership, to create historical geodata for studying the city's 18th-century landscape.

projects.title: The Cultural Microscope
projects.summary: Design and build a prototype interface to explore 'memes' (replicated visual elements) across tens of thousands of digitised historical maps, using digital embeddings and IIIF images, and allowing switching between visual elements and their source maps.

projects.title: The Hidden Grammar of Art History
projects.summary: Work with OCR extracted from about 300,000 digitised art-historical cardboards (Replica project) to realign artist name entities and derive heuristics about the grammar of artist attribution. An associated paper is planned.

projects.title: The Origins of Venice
projects.summary: Create a digital urban atlas of Venice for 1100 and 1350 from OCR-processed historiographical sources, and use it to analyse land ownership and land uses. The goal includes an interactive Leaflet cartography and statistical analysis of ownership, land use and family names.

projects.title: The space of Victorian London
projects.summary: Study how 19th and 20th century urban interventions affected the social-spatial structure of London, by enriching an 1890s Ordnance Survey building and text dataset with infrastructure and economic data and linking it to social class data from Booth's map.

projects.title: The World as a Canvas: Multimodal Realignment of Historical Map Archives
projects.summary: Develop a multimodal method to georeference historical maps at scale by combining textual cues and latent image representations from a domain-specific vision foundation model, matching map features to contemporary geodata via keypoints and graph neural networks.

projects.title: Deep Learning image reconstruction of cones free-running cardiac MRI
projects.summary: Master's project in cardiovascular MRI on deep learning image reconstruction for free-running cardiac MRI acquired with cones trajectories. Location is CHUV Biopôle, Lausanne.

projects.title: Fast metabolic imaging by magnetic resonance fingerprinting
projects.summary: Master or semester project on fast metabolic imaging using magnetic resonance fingerprinting at EPFL CIBM, Lausanne.

projects.title: Functional magnetic resonance spectroscopy at 7 Tesla
projects.summary: Master or semester project on functional magnetic resonance spectroscopy at 7 Tesla at EPFL CIBM, Lausanne.

projects.title: Novel hardware technologies for neuroimaging and neurostimulation
projects.summary: Master or semester project on novel hardware technologies for neuroimaging and neurostimulation at EPFL CIBM, Lausanne.

projects.title: Optimisation of the process pipeline of cerebrovascular reactivity data for clinical research
projects.summary: Master project to optimise the processing pipeline for cerebrovascular reactivity data used in clinical research. Location is HUG, CIBM MRI HUG-UNIGE, Geneva.

projects.title: Dynamic wetting measurement with image analysis on synchrotron x-ray tomography data
projects.summary: Measure dynamic wetting using image analysis applied to synchrotron X-ray tomography data.

projects.title: Event detection by signal processing to characterize optical fiber
projects.summary: Detect events in signals by signal processing to characterize an optical fiber.

projects.title: Learning Molecular Anisotropic Diffusion with Self-Supervised Deep Learning
projects.summary: Learn molecular anisotropic diffusion using self-supervised deep learning.

projects.title: Python software development for automated single-cell protein isolation with a CryoWriter
projects.summary: Develop Python software to automate single-cell protein isolation with a CryoWriter.

projects.title: Semester Project: X-ray reconstruction corrections for mechanics and biology
projects.summary: Develop corrections for X-ray reconstruction applied to mechanics and biology data.

projects.title: AI and Agentic Driven Generation of State-of-the-Art Branch Predictors
projects.summary: Use AI and agentic systems to automatically generate state-of-the-art branch predictors.

projects.title: Learning Atmospheric Similarity for Retrieval-Augmented Weather Forecasting
projects.summary: Learn atmospheric similarity to support retrieval-augmented weather forecasting.

projects.title: MSc thesis: Evaluating explainable machine learning tools for understanding greenhouse gas flux time series
projects.summary: Evaluate explainable machine learning tools for interpreting greenhouse gas flux time series. This is a master's thesis offer.

projects.title: MSc thesis: Uncertainty-aware deep learning for large-scale mapping of mass movements using SAR interferometry
projects.summary: Develop uncertainty-aware deep learning methods to map mass movements at large scale using SAR interferometry. This is a master's thesis offer.

projects.title: Post-Training Quantization of Weather Foundation Models: Attention Quantization and Long-Rollout Calibration
projects.summary: Apply post-training quantization to weather foundation models, focusing on attention quantization and calibration for long autoregressive rollouts.

projects.title: Semester Project or Master Thesis: Flow Matching for Imaging Inverse Problems with Nonlinear Forward Operators
projects.summary: Develop flow matching generative models to solve imaging inverse problems with nonlinear forward operators. The project is offered as a semester project or master thesis for EPFL and ETH Zurich students.

projects.title: Synthetic Data Generation and Quality Assessment for the Mountain Biodiversity Knowledge Graph
projects.summary: Generate synthetic data for the Mountain Biodiversity Knowledge Graph and assess its quality.

projects.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Therapy Planning and Design
projects.summary: Proposed master thesis or semester project on applying generative AI to therapy planning and design.

projects.title: Large-Scale Frontier Model for High-Dimensional Biological Imaging Data
projects.summary: Proposed master thesis on building a large-scale frontier model for high-dimensional biological imaging data.

projects.title: Reasoning in Biological Foundation Models
projects.summary: Proposed master thesis on reasoning in biological foundation models.

projects.title: Vision-Language Models for Biomedicine
projects.summary: Proposed master thesis on vision-language models applied to biomedicine.

projects.title: AI agents that foster learners' critical thinking through argumentation
projects.summary: Student project on AI agents designed to foster learners' critical thinking through argumentation.

projects.title: Designing real-time AI support for collaborative, inquiry-based science learning
projects.summary: Student project on designing real-time AI support for collaborative, inquiry-based science learning.

projects.title: Human-AI co-orchestration of group collaborative argumentation and ideation
projects.summary: Student project on human-AI co-orchestration to support group collaborative argumentation and ideation.

projects.title: Human-AI interactions that preserve and elevate human expertise in AI-augmented work
projects.summary: Student project on designing human-AI interactions that preserve and elevate human expertise in AI-augmented work.

projects.title: Interactive tools to prepare citizens for democratic deliberation and policy co-creation
projects.summary: Student project on interactive tools that help citizens prepare for democratic deliberation and policy co-creation.

projects.title: Participatory and community-based approaches to AI development
projects.summary: Student project on participatory and community-based approaches to AI development.

projects.title: Worker-centred design of workplace AI systems
projects.summary: Student project on designing workplace AI systems centred on the needs of workers.

projects.title: Optimization, Formalization and Benchmarking
projects.summary: Student projects on optimization, formalization, and benchmarking of proof system components and techniques, which can be tailored to the student's experience and interests. Interested students are asked to email the contact with their CV.

projects.title: Zero knowledge succinct arguments, probabilistic proofs and complexity theory
projects.summary: Student projects on zero knowledge succinct arguments, probabilistic proofs and complexity theory, which can be tailored to the student's experience and interests. Interested students are asked to email the contact with their CV.

projects.title: 3D Surface reconstruction using 3D Gaussians and SDF
projects.summary: The project aims to build primitives so that a surface can be obtained from a 3D Gaussian scene with minimal extra computational cost, building on methods such as SuGaR and hybrid approaches that train a neural SDF alongside 3D Gaussians. Objectives are a literature review and experiments with different SDF formulations.

projects.title: Applied Deep Learning for Computer Aided Engineering
projects.summary: Students work on one of CVLab's deep learning problems for computer-aided engineering in aeronautics, such as object geometry parameterization, surrogate modeling of physical performance, or gradient-based optimization. The work is done in collaboration with aerodynamics experts at ISAE-SUPAERO.

projects.title: Computer Vision for Waste Management
projects.summary: Develop a computer vision solution for WasteFlow's SaaS that helps recycling facilities characterize waste mix, measure sorting efficiency, and detect performance loss. Possible tasks include real-time detection and classification of waste on conveyor belts, mass estimation, purity assessment, and foreign material identification, with optional deployment on edge devices.

projects.title: Efficient Diffusion Models via Quantization and Compression
projects.summary: The project aims to explore and systematically evaluate quantization and compression methods (INT8/INT4, mixed-precision, pruning, low-rank factorization, distillation) for diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion. The goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements while preserving generative quality, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices.

projects.title: Interpretable and Controllable Neural Shape Parameterizations
projects.summary: The project aims to build on DeepGeo to develop methods that make neural shape parameterizations more interpretable, controllable, and efficient to optimize. Research questions include automatically constructing parameter directions for geometric properties (e.g. airfoil thickness, camber, wing twist), keeping controls reliable under large deformations, and designing compact, adaptive parameter spaces that improve optimization convergence.

projects.title: Real-Time 3D Tracking and Anomaly Detection for Maritime Kite Systems
projects.summary: Integrate and calibrate a second camera to build a stereovision setup for 3D tracking of an automated kite wing used for maritime propulsion. The project then moves to real-time hardware processing, anomaly detection (e.g. tears, abnormal trajectories), and linking vision outputs to safety control actions.

projects.title: Recovering Thin Structures in 3D Foundation Models
projects.summary: The project aims to improve the performance of transformer-based 3D foundation models, such as Depth Anything 3, on thin structures, which are poorly handled due to the rough patchification of transformers. The student will investigate how to improve the model's performance on these thin structures.

projects.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Flight Dynamics
projects.summary: The research project aims to explore self-supervised methods, such as Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA), for learning aircraft dynamics from sensor measurements, with a focus on making the learned models useful for control. The student will propose and test new approaches on simulated flight data and potentially real measurements from the lab's experimental aircraft.

projects.title: Structured 3D Shape Optimization with Part-Based Implicit Neural Representations
projects.summary: The project aims to extend the part-based implicit representation PartSDF to engineering-driven 3D shape representation and optimization under constraints. Goals include structured multi-part representations, enforcing physical and design constraints (e.g. aerodynamics or structural efficiency), and scalable architectures for many-part objects.

projects.title: Accelerating Safe ML Systems
projects.summary: Explores how to use RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) communication to make distributed machine learning training both fast and secure, for example secure collaborative or robust ML training.

projects.title: Distributed Resource Efficient Inference Engine
projects.summary: Projects on the distributed inference engine Anyd, which aggregates heterogeneous hardware over any network into a unified cluster that schedules GenAI inference and handles failures transparently. The goal is to address the challenges of its distributed, automatically managed nature.

projects.title: Scalable Distributed Cache Coherency
projects.summary: Investigates how to reduce the communication overhead of distributed cache coherency protocols while keeping their performance, so that they scale to large distributed systems.

projects.title: Audio Processing - LARS
projects.summary: Add audio capabilities to the LARS real-time music system, including computing hardware delays and extracting audio features such as beat tracking and key finding. The project requires signal processing and low-latency real-time programming skills.

projects.title: Perceptual abilities of musical experts
projects.summary: Replicate existing behavioural music perception experiments with top-level performing artists to test how their perceptual abilities differ from those of previously studied participants. The project involves critically updating the original study's methods, implementing an online version, and analysing the data.

projects.title: Performance Optimization & Benchmarking - LARS
projects.summary: Improve the real-time performance and scalability of the LARS system by profiling it, optimizing critical C++ code paths, and addressing threading and concurrency issues. The project also involves building benchmarking tools and automating performance regression tests.

projects.title: Python Utilities to C++ Core Migration - LARS
projects.summary: Move key utilities of the LARS system from Python to optimized modern C++, including the C++ version of its pattern language for algorithmic composition. The work includes testing and benchmarking the translated code and maintaining the Python bindings via nanobind.

projects.title: Testing & Quality Assurance (C++ & Python) - LARS
projects.summary: Improve the reliability and maintainability of the LARS real-time interactive music system by designing a comprehensive test suite (unit, integration, regression, load tests) for its C++ and Python components. The project also includes setting up CI automated testing workflows and defining testing standards for plugins.

projects.title: Web development for graphic music analysis app
projects.summary: Develop the web interface of the lab's reductive music analysis app, which lets researchers express music analyses as graphs embedded in MEI music scores. Students can either rewrite the serverless web app in type-safe code with a modern event-driven JavaScript framework, or add features and fix bugs in the existing legacy code base.

projects.title: Coercion-resistant proof of personhood as a foundation for digital democracy
projects.summary: Prototype, test, and evaluate a coercion-resistance mechanism for e-voting in the context of in-person pseudonym parties, including a barebones web or mobile app and an informal usability study with volunteers. The goal is a detailed report, ideally leading to a research paper.

projects.title: Paradox-resistant reasoning in automated theorem provers
projects.summary: Help formalize, validate, and metalogically reason about Grounded Deduction, a non-classical logic foundation that allows unrestricted recursive definitions while defusing semantic paradoxes. Work uses a proof assistant or automated theorem prover such as Isabelle, Coq, or Lean, and optionally a grounded set theory in the LISA prover.

projects.title: Writing and editing tools based on matchertext and MinML
projects.summary: Develop tools and refine the MinML markup language, which is based on the matchertext syntactic discipline for cross-language embedding. Possible work includes integrating MinML authoring into existing Web and other tools, or designing a LaTeX-like MinML document language.

projects.title: 3D Question Answering at City-Scale: Multimodal LLMs
projects.summary: Implement a 3D multimodal LLM for question answering over city-scale 3D models using aligned historical data from Time Atlas. The model is to be integrated into the Time Atlas software.

projects.title: AI-Assisted Authority Files & Validation Dashboard (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, on AI-assisted workflows for authority files and a validation dashboard for the Armenian epigraphic data.

projects.title: Analysing Layout Elements of Historical Maps
projects.summary: Detect map layout elements such as cartouches, scale bars, wind roses and illustrations in a dataset of about 400,000 historical maps, then cluster them by author, region and period.

projects.title: Annotation of Culture-Specific Data for LLM Evaluation Using the Psychosocial Categorisation Model (PSCM)
projects.summary: Build a bilingual (Armenian-English) dataset of culturally embedded expressions, annotated with the PSCM schema. The annotated data is used to evaluate LLM and MT performance on culture-specific meaning.

projects.title: Armenian Editorial Signs Converter (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, on converting Armenian editorial signs in the epigraphic data.

projects.title: Armenian Epigraphy and Cultural Heritage Data Analysis
projects.summary: Collect and clean a selection of books on epigraphy and cultural heritage, store them in a database, and extract key terms and themes with NLP techniques, with a focus on Armenian inscriptions.

projects.title: Bias analysis of cultural heritage manipulation classification of Wikipedia edits by LLMs
projects.summary: Analyse biases of open-source LLMs when classifying Wikipedia edits about Armenian and Ukrainian cultural heritage as manipulative, using a human-labelled ground truth. The project also explores bias mitigation strategies such as prompt engineering and multi-agent setups.

projects.title: Biology of a VLM: Transcoder Training for Multimodal Interpretability
projects.summary: Train a transcoder replacement model for a vision-language model and use it to analyse the model's internal reasoning, including modality-unified concept features and reasoning on text-heavy documents.

projects.title: Converging Conceptual Abstraction in Self-Supervised Models
projects.summary: Develop a representation-convergence technique that compares the conceptual abstractions learned by sparse autoencoders or cross-layer transcoders across self-supervised models. The project examines transfer of these abstractions between models.

projects.title: Data Visualization Dashboard for Monitoring and Quality Control of Large-Scale Data Processing
projects.summary: Build a lightweight, modular dashboard that shows the stages of the Impresso data processing pipeline and supports monitoring and quality control.

projects.title: Dense Language Encoders for Agglomerative Models
projects.summary: Build a dense text encoder that aligns language with the dense features of agglomerative vision models such as EUPE. The goal is zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation by cosine similarity.

projects.title: Detection, Linking, and Georeferencing of Place Names in Historical Newspapers
projects.summary: Scale multilingual location detection and georeferencing, with a focus on sub-city levels, across the Impresso historical newspaper corpus. The work includes relevance filtering and evaluation.

projects.title: Discovering Historical Events Through Spatio-Temporal Analysis
projects.summary: Design and prototype a reproducible, unsupervised spatiotemporal anomaly-detection pipeline that surfaces historically significant events in the Flickr Commons archive. The project is carried out with the Flickr Foundation.

projects.title: Driving Representation Convergence using Image Aesthetics
projects.summary: Test whether aesthetic images produce representations and representational geometry distinct from non-aesthetic images, and whether aesthetics drives cross-model convergence. The project includes building an international, historically balanced aesthetics dataset.

projects.title: EPFL Digital Twin Foundation Model
projects.summary: Prototype a first foundation model of the EPFL campus by aligning heterogeneous datasets (3D structures, occupancy, food, mobility, schedules) into a unified spatiotemporal representation. The model is intended for forecasting and counterfactual simulation.

projects.title: EpiDoc Corpus Creation & Geolocation (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, which structures the Armenian epigraphic corpus of India (IndiaArmEpiC) in TEI/EpiDoc. This project covers corpus creation and geolocation.

projects.title: Evaluating the Novelty of Knowledge in Texts with Large Language Models
projects.summary: Develop algorithms that assess whether historical texts contain knowledge that was not already present in an LLM's pretraining data. The work combines novelty detection with retrieval approaches.

projects.title: Exploring Large Vision Models for Historical Newspaper Segmentation
projects.summary: Evaluate large vision models for segmenting and labelling logical layout units (titles, text paragraphs, tables, images) on historical newspaper pages from the Impresso corpus.

projects.title: Exploring the structure of the Venetian urban fabric with 3-dimensional isovists
projects.summary: Analyse the structure of Venetian urban space using three-dimensional isovists.

projects.title: Geolocating Artworks
projects.summary: Develop methods that use vision-language models and multimodal embeddings to identify the places depicted in paintings, engravings and illustrations. The goal is to link artworks to spatial entities in the Time Atlas.

projects.title: Identification and Classification of Maps in Historical Newspapers
projects.summary: Train a binary map vs. non-map image classifier on Impresso newspaper pages, then a classifier for the country or region a map represents.

projects.title: IIIF Document Information Extraction for Time Atlas
projects.summary: Build a pipeline that fetches manuscript images through IIIF, transcribes and structures them with language-vision models, and extracts named entities and spatiotemporal information. The results are prepared for integration into Time Atlas.

projects.title: Mapping Newspapers: Creation of a database of Swiss historical newspapers based on Blaser's bibliography
projects.summary: Extract the semi-structured information of Fritz Blaser's Swiss Press Bibliography (1956) into a lightweight database describing Swiss newspapers from 1803 to 1958. The database supports the Impresso web application and studies of the Swiss press.

projects.title: News Articles in Space and Time
projects.summary: A semester project on news articles in space and time.

projects.title: Pleiades Integration into the TimeAtlas
projects.summary: Design and prototype the integration of the Pleiades gazetteer of ancient places into the Time Atlas infrastructure. The work includes data mapping, ingestion pipelines and visualization of ancient places.

projects.title: Preparing and Evaluating Vintage Language Models
projects.summary: Prepare the methodological and technical foundations for Vintage LLMs, language models trained only on pre-modern historical corpora. The work covers corpus construction, contamination control, synthetic data and historically grounded evaluation benchmarks.

projects.title: Preparing Historical Data for Apertus
projects.summary: Collect, filter, clean, normalize and document historical and cultural heritage corpora for a future training cycle of the open Apertus language model. The work covers OCR quality, metadata, deduplication and contamination filtering.

projects.title: Projecting Representations of Beauty
projects.summary: Build a pseudo-labelling pipeline that projects aesthetic labels from image assessment models onto 3D scenes, and train a model to predict aesthetic labels from point cloud structure alone.

projects.title: Reconstructing the Past: Generating 3D Models of Lost Buildings from Stylistically Diverse Inputs with Geometry Transformers
projects.summary: Test feed-forward geometry transformers (MapAnything, VGGT, NOVA3R) on natural and stylized images, then fine-tune the best model. The final aim is to generate 3D models of lost buildings from DHLAB historical image collections.

projects.title: Reconstructing the topology of Venetian domestic space through cadastral analysis
projects.summary: Reconstruct the topology of domestic space in Venice from cadastral records.

projects.title: Semi-automated historical GIS construction for Venetian secondary sources
projects.summary: Build a historical GIS from Venetian secondary sources using semi-automated methods.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Hierarchical Reconstruction
projects.summary: Investigate methods for creating object-part hierarchies in city-scale 3D data, derived from per-point open-vocabulary labels, including hyperbolic embeddings. It is part of a SwissAI-funded project.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Human Interaction
projects.summary: Design user interfaces for interacting with large-scale 3D scenes, including 3D-native and multimodal querying, and RAG-style chat with MLLMs. The work is to be integrated with the Time Atlas beta.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Implicit Reconstruction
projects.summary: Prepare datasets and pipelines and research neural reconstruction methods for egocentric semantic understanding, as part of a SwissAI-funded open-vocabulary 3D model for city-scale scenes.

projects.title: Standalone Web Visualisation (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, on a standalone web visualisation of the Armenian epigraphic data.

projects.title: Tarot Deck Motif Analysis
projects.summary: Prepare the corpus, data model and an initial taxonomy of visual motifs for analysing historical Tarot decks, and prototype computer-vision tools to detect and classify recurring motifs. The project is run with the University of Lausanne.

projects.title: Temporal Language Models and the Dynamics of Language Change
projects.summary: Study and extend temporal language model approaches inspired by TLM-1 to model semantic drift, narrative evolution and temporal forecasting. The work uses diachronic corpora such as newspapers, books or archives.

projects.title: The Social Life of Images: Using Social Metadata to Enhance AI Generated Descriptions of Digital Image Archives
projects.summary: Develop and evaluate methods that combine image-to-text models with social metadata (tags, comments, galleries) from Flickr Commons to produce richer descriptions of archival images. The project is carried out with the Flickr Foundation.

projects.title: Tracking the Weaponization and Manipulation of Cultural Heritage in Armenia
projects.summary: Retrieve and analyse Wikipedia editing histories, talk pages and related content to monitor how cultural heritage narratives about Armenia are manipulated. Findings are intended to support documentation and heritage protection.

projects.title: Tracking the Weaponization and Manipulation of Cultural Heritage in Ukraine by Russia
projects.summary: Analyse Wikipedia editing histories, talk pages and content about Ukrainian cultural heritage to monitor politically motivated manipulation. Findings are intended to support heritage protection and policy.

projects.title: Typological analysis of Venetian floor plans through Computer Vision
projects.summary: Use computer vision to analyse and classify the typologies of Venetian floor plans.

projects.title: VLM Finetuning for Accurate Features from Images of Degraded Point Clouds
projects.summary: Evaluate how base vision-language models perform on synthetic renderings of sparse point clouds versus real images, then fine-tune them to produce embeddings closer to those of real images.

projects.title: What's in those millions of images? Generating accurate descriptions for 4 million historical newspaper images
projects.summary: Generate and evaluate textual descriptions of roughly 4 million Impresso newspaper images by comparing vision-language models. The work includes building a test set and defining evaluation criteria.

projects.title: World Model Semantic Surprise as a Measure for Multimodal Urban Incongruity
projects.summary: Develop embedding-space semantic trajectory tools and apply them to urban trajectories from driving videos, street-view imagery, LiDAR or building text. The aim is to measure violation of expectation as an indicator of urban incongruity.

projects.title: Cost models & tuning the query optimizer of a JIT analytical engine
projects.summary: The student will become familiar with Apache Calcite and model the cost of the operators of Proteus, an in-house analytical DBMS engine. The goal is cost models that let the optimizer reason about parallelization and resource allocation, and an auto-tuning infrastructure to select cost-model hyper-parameters for different machines. The project lasts 14 weeks.

projects.title: Efficient Concurrent Interval Container for Multicore Systems
projects.summary: Design and implement a concurrent interval container inspired by the Boost Interval Container Library, with an index layout and synchronization protocol supporting concurrent overlap and containment queries and atomic updates. The prototype will be evaluated against a global-lock sequential container and concurrent-index baselines on throughput, latency, scalability and memory.

projects.title: Limiting interference of code generation to analytical query execution through remote JIT-ing
projects.summary: The project studies how just-in-time code generation interferes with analytical query execution in the Proteus DBMS, and quantifies the resulting slowdown. It then explores running code generation remotely on a separate, possibly smaller machine to isolate it from query execution, measuring the effect on query latency and throughput. The project is 14 weeks long.

projects.title: Memory-Aware Hash Joins for Heterogeneous Memory Environments
projects.summary: The project studies the design space of hash join implementations in heterogeneous memory environments such as CXL memory. The student will evaluate existing hash joins, analyze the design space, and propose memory-aware hash join design choices evaluated on SSB and TPC-H.

projects.title: Understanding and Mitigating Real-World Global Serializability Violations
projects.summary: The project studies global serializability violations in multi-database transactions of microservice applications. The student will empirically study 2-3 open-source microservice applications, integrate existing mitigation methods (e.g. Sonata, the Ticket method, ad hoc synchronization), and evaluate their performance.

projects.title: Extracting Block I/O Stream Representations from Filesystems
projects.summary: Investigate how filesystems (e.g., ext4, XFS, F2FS, Btrfs) transform application file operations into block I/O seen by SSDs, and derive a minimal set of block I/O streams that captures the steady-state device-level behavior relevant to SSD performance and write amplification.

projects.title: Profiling Automated Verifiers
projects.summary: Build a profiler that attributes SMT-based verifier solving time (e.g., Dafny, KLEE with Z3/CVC5) across the verifier stack, distinguishes useful from useless work and brute-force search from precise reasoning, and evaluates whether it helps pinpoint real-world performance root causes.

projects.title: SSD-Aware RL for Data Placement in Storage Systems
projects.summary: Study whether exposing SSD-internal state (garbage collection activity, write amplification, utilization, wear) to a reinforcement-learning data-placement agent, and optimizing jointly for performance, write amplification, wear balance and energy, yields better policies for heterogeneous SSD arrays than existing black-box approaches.

projects.title: Beyond the Strings: LLM-Based Knowledge Extraction for Historical Puppetry Knowledge Graphs
projects.summary: Evaluate LLM-based extraction of historical relationships and scholarly interpretations from a small corpus of theatrical and archival texts on Sophie Taeuber-Arp's 1918 König Hirsch marionettes, comparing how models separate historical facts from interpretations and map them to a predefined ontology for knowledge graphs.

projects.title: Evaluation Framework for Cross-Domain Visual Retrieval in Cultural Heritage Image Collections
projects.summary: Build a rigorous, reproducible evaluation framework for cross-domain visual retrieval and UMAP-based visualization tools applied to cultural heritage image collections, including the Murten Panorama and 15th-century manuscripts. The work covers dataset survey, generative construction of evaluation sets, and benchmarking of retrieval accuracy and visualization fidelity.

projects.title: Generative Workflow for Navigable 3D Worlds from a Large-Scale Panoramic Painting
projects.summary: Develop a reproducible generative AI workflow that turns segments of a large panoramic painting (the 1893 Murten Panorama) into navigable 3D scenes using world models and 3D asset generation, with scenes placed on a geolocated terrain map for VR/XR heritage experiences.
skills: generative AI tools for images and 3D

projects.title: Computational Design with Multiple Tension Elements: Elastic Cables and Sheets with Elastic Rod Structures
projects.summary: The project studies how cables and sheet patches can be treated as interchangeable and combinable tension elements that shape elastic rods into target curves. The student will build on an existing cable-to-patch conversion prototype and a C++/Python framework, addressing open questions on form-finding, evaluation, intersection-free layout and topology optimization.

projects.title: Inverse design of highly curved surfaces for surface-based inflatables
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a parameterization method for highly curved surfaces that respects the contraction bounds of surface-based inflatables by using cone singularities. Key questions include optimizing cone placement and angles under scale-factor bounds, realizing the resulting cuts physically, and measuring how much the achievable shape range is extended compared with existing methods.

projects.title: Simulation and Design of Transformable Elastic Linkages
projects.summary: Explore how elastic beams and joints can be designed and connected to achieve desired transformations, shapes, and functions, such as deployable shells and grid-shell-like structures (X-Shell, C-Shell, BamX). The work aims to simulate the behaviour of elastic linkage systems and develop new ones guided by geometric insight, combining parametric modeling, physics-based simulation, numerical optimization, inverse design and possibly physical prototyping. Students may propose their own research directions.

projects.title: Tencer Metamaterials: Unit Cell Generation and Rigid Motion Analysis
projects.summary: Design new classes of mechanical metamaterial unit cells built from tencers (tension-constrained elastic rods). The student will develop an automatic tool that generates diverse candidate unit-cell topologies for simulation, and a strategy to refine designs so that no undesired relative rigid motion is possible between components.

projects.title: Improving Coverage Reliability in Cortex-M Firmware Rehosting
projects.summary: Studies whether coverage reported by Cortex-M firmware rehosting systems reflects meaningful exploration, or is affected by artifacts of the emulated environment such as MMIO, interrupts, timers and DMA. The project will build a framework to record coverage with execution context and develop techniques to improve coverage-guided fuzzing of rehosted firmware.

projects.title: Ownership-Aware Bug Hunting in Rust Crates
projects.summary: Aims to build an ownership-aware bug detection mechanism for Rust crates that models ownership transitions induced by unsafe APIs, such as bitwise copies that lead to double-free bugs. The goal is to detect ownership-related bugs the compiler cannot enforce.

projects.title: Accelerating ecological connectivity analysis with graph neural networks
projects.summary: Proposes using graph neural networks to learn coarser graph embeddings of fine-scale landscape features, so that resistance distance-based gene flow predictions become computationally tractable at higher spatial resolution. Directions include graph coarsening strategies, approximation error bounds, and validation on synthetic and real ecological data.

projects.title: Finding Slow Components in a Graph
projects.summary: The project studies how many random shortest-path distance queries are needed to identify a set of vertices V_1 whose incident edge weights are much larger than the rest of a weighted graph with exponentially distributed weights. It includes simulations on a range of graphs, evaluation of accuracy and sample complexity, and theoretical accuracy bounds.

projects.title: High-performance differentiable AMG in JAX with GPU acceleration
projects.summary: Develop an algebraic multigrid (AMG) solver in JAX that supports automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration, for scientific machine learning workflows requiring differentiable iterative linear solves. The work involves analysing existing Python and Julia AMG implementations and designing a JAX-compatible architecture.

projects.title: Reusable Foundations for Probabilistic Proofs in Lean
projects.summary: Develop a reusable Lean library on top of Mathlib providing foundations for probability (beyond existing martingales, concentration inequalities and CLT, e.g. Markov chains, random walks, couplings), so probabilists can formalize their results more easily. If time allows, the library would be used to formalize a paper on random graphs and branching processes.

projects.title: Dataset Acquisition for Low-Light Image Denoising
projects.summary: Capture a new dataset of noisy/clean image pairs and dark calibration frames at many exposure times to extend the 2-Shots in the Dark low-light denoising method. The student would sort and preprocess the data and publish it on Hugging Face with a dataset card.

projects.title: Accelerate FPGA Implementation Time
projects.summary: Reduce the FPGA bitstream implementation time generated from high-level synthesis code, from several minutes to a few seconds.

projects.title: Hardware coherence on various wishbone bus-architectures
projects.summary: Design and implement software-configurable hardware cache coherence protocols (such as MSI and MESI) on wishbone shared, crossbar and ring bus architectures, for a system based on Hazard3 RISC-V CPUs.

projects.title: Low-Level Optimization of Dynamically Scheduled Circuits
projects.summary: Optimise dynamically scheduled circuits after the DHLS compiler output, working on RTL-to-physical FPGA implementation in Vivado during logic synthesis and place-and-route to account for real routing delays and congestion.

projects.title: Open-Source Work on Dynamic High-level Synthesis Compiler Targeting FPGAs
projects.summary: Contribute to Dynamatic, an open-source dynamic high-level synthesis compiler built on MLIR that generates RTL for FPGAs from C/C++. Work can cover compiler passes at different lowering levels, or debugging, visualisation and benchmarking tools; contributions are intended to become part of the codebase.

projects.title: Optimizing place and route for high frequency task parallel FPGA accelerators
projects.summary: Increase the clock frequency of HardCilk-generated FPGA circuits by adding elastic buffers to their ready-valid interfaces, and analyse the results using Vivado place and route.

projects.title: Postquantum Cryptography Core Using High-Level Synthesis
projects.summary: Explore and improve the quality of results of post-quantum cryptography hardware cores produced with high-level synthesis, compared with RTL-based designs.

projects.title: SOC-graphical configurator as VS-code plug-in
projects.summary: Develop a VS Code plug-in that provides a graphical tool for composing OpenRisc-based SoC designs for the CS-473 and CS-476 courses, generating top-level Verilog and memory maps, and exporting designs as TikZ pictures and PDF.

projects.title: Toward Coarse-Grained Field Programmable Gate Arrays
projects.summary: Study a coarser-grained, word-level version of FPGAs and evaluate its performance as a reconfigurable computing fabric, including compiler optimisations, architectural ideas, and physical implementation and modelling.

projects.title: A Digital Twin for collective decision making
projects.summary: Build on an existing pipeline that fits Digital Twins to zebrafish behaviour recorded in response to virtual conspecifics. The project starts with an auto-regressive generative model as a baseline, then uses interpretable approaches to understand fish decision making, ideally producing predictions testable in real animals.

projects.title: Implementing and extending a biologically inspired computational model of spatial navigation in rodents
projects.summary: Implement in code a rodent navigation model with a taxon pathway (visual input to motor actions via dorsal striatum-like mechanisms) and a locale pathway (grid and place cells feeding the ventral striatum). Validate the model in reorientation and watermaze paradigms, then extend it in several possible directions.

projects.title: Modeling perceptual rules of social interactions in single animal virtual reality
projects.summary: Use computational modelling and machine learning on existing zebrafish behaviour recordings from dots projected on a screen to test whether visual preference for a virtual conspecific arises from hard-wired motion tuning or from coupling to the fish's own swim cycle. If time permits, the models will be extended to predict neural signals in the fish brain.

projects.title: Training spiking networks to generate fast time-varying patterns
projects.summary: Investigates whether spiking networks of SRM0 neurons with escape noise can be trained, using FORCE-type online learning and exact population rate equations, to produce fast and complex time-varying patterns. The project also explores which kinds of patterns can be learned when there are no constraints on the speed of the dynamics.
skills: strong background in mathematics, physics or computer science

projects.title: When is a good predictor a good model?
projects.summary: Investigates which model-brain comparison metrics, stimuli and experiments can distinguish artificial neural networks that truly share the brain's mechanisms from those that only predict neural activity well. The student will record from networks that solve the same task with the same or different mechanisms, apply metrics such as linear predictivity, RSA and CKA, and test whether lesions predict effects on the target system.

projects.title: Message passing for quantum models (SMILS)
projects.summary: Develop message passing techniques for simple quantum spin models on graphs, using functional integral and/or discrete phase space representations, with a focus on investigating topological phases.

projects.title: Quantum constraint satisfaction problems (SMILS)
projects.summary: The project investigates quantum versions of constraint satisfaction problems such as quantum K-SAT, aiming to determine the phase diagram as a function of constraint density and to find product-state ground states (PRODSAT phase) with algorithmic methods. It starts from a study of the basic literature on the topic.

projects.title: Universal prediction and alpha-mutual information
projects.summary: The project studies Alpha-NML predictors, a class of estimators interpolating between the Krichevsky-Trofimov (KT) and Normalized Maximum Likelihood (NML) estimators for universal prediction under log loss. Students would run experimental work (MATLAB or Python) to extend closed-form gamma-function formulas to longer sequences, derive formulas for non-i.i.d. sources such as Markov sources, and assess average-case performance compared with KT and NML.

projects.title: Analysing the Effect of Assistant Post-Training on Diversity and Sycophancy in Pedagogical LLMs
projects.summary: Studies how diversity, sycophancy and safety change across the post-training stages (base, SFT, DPO, RLVR) of the open model Olmo 3 7B when generating feedback on open-ended student work. The project aims to find internal features linked to these behaviours and to test lightweight interventions (weight interpolation, feature steering, short LoRA fine-tuning) that improve diversity and reduce sycophancy without undermining safety.

projects.title: Do Questions Trigger Misconceptions? Measuring When Student Misconceptions Show Up
projects.summary: Uses existing anonymised Eedi diagnostic maths responses to measure the trigger strength of each question-misconception pair and test whether it predicts when a student's misconception reappears, controlling for ability and difficulty. It also compares a persona-prompted open LLM simulator (e.g. Qwen3-8B) with real students' misconception rates.

projects.title: Mapping Failures of AI Agents on Educational Tasks
projects.summary: Analyses a dataset of agent interactions across six learning contexts to map failures of agentic AI systems on education tasks (understanding the learning context and modelling learner data) to generic failure taxonomies. The goal is to develop an education-specific coding scheme, combine manual and LLM-based trace analysis, and identify where existing taxonomies need refinement.

projects.title: Robustness of LLM Reasoning Strategies for Educational Applications
projects.summary: Investigates how different reasoning strategies (linear, symbolic, reflective, iterative) affect the robustness and reliability of LLMs under controlled perturbations in educational tasks such as misconception detection and educational content generation. It evaluates accuracy, explanation consistency, error propagation, recovery and the trade-off with computational cost.

projects.title: Project 1: Comparing Representational Hierarchies in Neural Networks
projects.summary: Investigates how layer selection and aggregation shape conclusions about representational similarity between neural networks. The goal is a principled way to compare models across their full representational hierarchies, distinguishing isolated layer matches from agreement across the hierarchy, and reassessing evidence for representational convergence.

projects.title: Project 2: What Do Language Models Need from 3D Encoders?
projects.summary: Studies what 3D encoders (point clouds or Gaussian splats) contribute when connected to a language model for 3D scene reasoning, and how 3D representations could be learned to be more useful to LLMs. Starts from existing 3D encoders and a controlled 3D LLM pipeline, and extends to modeling spatial organization of cells.

projects.title: Project 3: Learning patient-level predictions from the spatial proteome
projects.summary: Develops a multiple instance learning approach for patient-level prediction from spatial single-cell proteomics data, aggregating information across spatial scales from single cells to niches and whole-tissue organization. Evaluation on public multiplexed imaging cohorts with patient-level outcomes such as cancer survival, including data efficiency and agreement of attended regions with known pathology.

projects.title: Project 4: Improving agents for single-cell genomics and biomedical discovery
projects.summary: Aims to improve the reasoning capabilities of LLM-based agents for single-cell biology tasks using agentic reinforcement learning, so that the agents can plan, execute computational workflows, and formulate hypotheses for biomedical discovery.

projects.title: AI safety evaluations feeding back into Apertus Posttraining
projects.summary: Work with UN agencies such as UNICC to incorporate findings from recent red-teaming studies into the posttraining recipes (safety SFT and RL) of the next generation Apertus model.

projects.title: Build decentralized LLMs in the browser
projects.summary: Practical project joining a larger team effort to build decentralized and federated training software in which many clients (e.g. phones or hospitals) collaboratively train models such as smaller LLMs while preserving data privacy; students would help integrate the Burn framework within DISCO.

projects.title: Communication-efficient gossip methods for replacing all-reduce in distributed LLM training
projects.summary: Implement decentralized pairwise averaging of model weights instead of all-to-all communication, and investigate how model and data parallelism settings and communication compression affect distributed LLM pre-training.

projects.title: Data curation and curriculum learning for pre-training, theory and practice
projects.summary: Semester project around LLM pre-training, covering data curation and curriculum learning, with both theoretical and practical components. Part of the MLO large language model project offer.

projects.title: Efficiency engineering for LLM pretraining and specifically MoE architectures
projects.summary: Semester project on improving the computational efficiency of LLM pre-training, with a focus on mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Improving factuality understanding for LLM training
projects.summary: Add a factuality tag or masking to each document to guide an LLM's understanding of what is factual, with the goal of enhancing factuality and reducing hallucinations; post-training techniques may also be investigated.

projects.title: Learning to sample on the fly for SGD / curriculum learning
projects.summary: Train an auxiliary network that assigns scores to training data points and use these scores to select an improved set of training points, exploring several ways of training the auxiliary parameters.

projects.title: LLM inference on old V100 GPUs
projects.summary: Aims to run recent large open-weight MoE models efficiently on the EPFL cluster of V100 GPUs and compare with newer GPU versions, applying quantization and communication-efficient parallelism with inference frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang in multi-GPU settings.

projects.title: LLM Pretraining Data Curation
projects.summary: Advance pre-training data curation beyond baselines such as FineWeb-2 HQ through new techniques for signal extraction, semantic filtering and partially synthetic augmentation or rephrasing, in English or multilingual settings. One idea is to study the impact of data quality on the curse of multilinguality and its relation to scaling laws.

projects.title: Novel architectures (including efficient long context or MoE related mechanisms)
projects.summary: Semester project on new LLM architectures, including efficient long-context and mixture-of-experts mechanisms. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Optimization dynamics for LLMs (e.g. Muon and AdEMAmix variants, and interactions with architecture)
projects.summary: Semester project studying optimization dynamics of LLM training, such as Muon and AdEMAmix variants and their interaction with architecture. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Safety and alignment during pretraining
projects.summary: Semester project on integrating safety and alignment considerations into LLM pre-training. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Scaling to longer context windows through modifications of attention
projects.summary: Semester project on extending the context length of LLMs by modifying the attention mechanism. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Tools-usage during pretraining & finetuning
projects.summary: Semester project on enabling tool usage by LLMs during pre-training and fine-tuning. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: AI TOOLS | Impact of glass-boxing the Machine Learning pipeline on learning
projects.summary: Develop a custom web-based platform to run a study comparing three levels of transparency (glass box, gray box, black box) in a decision-tree machine learning task where users predict a dinosaur's diet from field notes. The project adapts an existing paper-based experiment to a digital environment to test whether exposing data preparation or model logic improves understanding of ML.

projects.title: AI TOOLS – Understanding Learning Through Pipeline Transparency
projects.summary: Student project on AI tools for education, examining how pipeline transparency helps learners understand learning.

projects.title: Testing a neutrality-detection tool
projects.summary: Final pre-deployment testing of a tool that localizes where ISPs throttle, block, or de-prioritize traffic. The work includes running experiments on various networks, analyzing results to evaluate accuracy and robustness, and suggesting improvements.

projects.title: Using math to infer network behavior
projects.summary: Infer network behavior, such as traffic de-prioritization, using only external observations of a flow. The student would help reconstruct the queuing delay process seen by a flow from its own irregular observations.

projects.title: Improving the performance of ML workloads
projects.summary: Analyze and break down the software-stack overheads of ML inference and training, within a single machine and across machines, and propose optimizations to improve system performance.

projects.title: Performance Modeling of eBPF Programs
projects.summary: Design a scalable and accurate performance model for eBPF programs, to support performance quantification, debugging, and checking of eBPF kernel extensions against functionally equivalent baselines.

projects.title: Does Personalization in Medical Collaborative Learning Learn Site Shortcuts?
projects.summary: Investigates whether standard personalized federated learning methods learn site-specific shortcuts (spurious correlations) on medical data, with the goal of informing a personalization method that keeps useful site-specific features while avoiding shortcuts.

projects.title: Noise or Lies? Distinguishing privacy protection from fairwashing in black-box audits
projects.summary: Studies when an external auditor, who only sees black-box query answers, can distinguish an honest privacy-preserving platform (random, public noise) from a manipulative platform that performs fairwashing to hide discrimination.

projects.title: Privacy Vulnerability Transfer in Model Merging
projects.summary: Studies how privacy vulnerabilities, including membership inference and extraction risks, propagate into merged language models built with model merging and task arithmetic, and how merging coefficients, number of merged models and task similarity affect this transfer.

projects.title: Whose bubble is it? Harvesting idle capacity in data-parallel, expert-parallel LLM serving
projects.summary: Characterizes where GPU idle capacity arises in data-parallel, expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts LLM serving and determines when it can be harvested for parameter-efficient fine-tuning without violating service-level objectives through coupling between replicas.

projects.title: Message passing for Quantum Models
projects.summary: Develop message passing techniques for simple quantum spin models on graphs.

projects.title: Quantum constraint satisfaction problems
projects.summary: Investigate quantum versions of constraint satisfaction problems such as K-SAT, where N quantum bits (spin-1/2) are subject to M constraints acting on them.

projects.title: NET1: Recovering User Questions from the Web Traffic of AI Search and Crawling APIs
projects.summary: Studies whether network observers can infer or recover user prompts from the traffic generated when AI search and crawling APIs (such as Exa or Firecrawl) retrieve and scrape web content. The student builds a corpus of questions, runs them through these services under controlled conditions, and records the resulting network activity.

projects.title: SYS1: Empirical Threat Models in Censorship Circumvention
projects.summary: Examines why some censorship circumvention designs achieve large-scale success while others with strong theoretical potential have had no practical impact. The project takes a cryptographic threat-modelling perspective on empirical censorship behaviour and deployed circumvention tools.
