projects.title: Analysis of dendritic spine changes using deep-learning encoding in a latent space
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a deep-learning system that reconstructs the temporal evolution of dendritic spine shapes. Spine shapes from time-lapse 3D microscopy would be encoded into a low-dimensional latent space to classify single-spine behaviours and study neural plasticity.

projects.title: Automated image analysis of tau fibrils in the human Alzheimer's disease brain
projects.summary: The project aims to detect tau fibrils within tau tangles in human Alzheimer's disease brain tissue, imaged with correlative light and electron microscopy, and measure their twist to study tangle stages. The student would develop a Python image analysis workflow for denoising, line detection, segmentation and machine learning-based pixel classification.

projects.title: Continuous-Domain Phase Retrieval in Dimension One
projects.summary: Develop and benchmark a coarse-to-fine (multiscale) numerical solver for recovering a complex-valued continuous-domain signal from magnitude-only linear measurements. The solver starts with Wirtinger Flow at a coarse scale and propagates estimates up the resolution hierarchy, and is compared with single-scale Wirtinger Flow with spectral initialization at full resolution.

projects.title: Exploring Global Youth Art Through AI: A Semantic Analysis of the IMAJ Collection
projects.summary: Semantic analysis of a database of more than 100,000 drawings by young artists aged 3 to 25 from 150 countries, collected by IMAJ. The project will evaluate large language models on curated subsets before scaling up to generate textual interpretations and enrich the metadata of the collection.

projects.title: Generating of Point-Spread Function for Advanced Imaging Microscopy in Python
projects.summary: Proposed student project to generate point-spread functions for advanced imaging microscopy, implemented in Python.

projects.title: Geometry of Images: A War Between Fastness and Expressiveness
projects.summary: Proposed project on the trade-off between speed and expressiveness in image geometry models.

projects.title: High-Dimensional Gaussian Sampling: Cholesky versus Markov
projects.summary: Compares three approaches to generating high-dimensional Gaussian samples: exact Cholesky-factorization linear algebra, iterative Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and Perturb-and-Map. The goal is to find the best trade-off between computational speed and statistical accuracy for large-scale inverse problems.

projects.title: Sampling from Learned Regularizers
projects.summary: The project studies posterior sampling for linear inverse problems using energy-based models built from learnable potential functions applied to linear filter responses. The goal is to implement and analyze sampling algorithms such as the (annealed) Metropolis adjusted Langevin algorithm for uncertainty quantification.

projects.title: Training Complex-Valued Denoisers for Phase Retrieval
projects.summary: The project aims to train a denoiser that operates directly on complex-valued data, regularizing magnitude and phase jointly for phase retrieval. The student will study amplitude-phase coupling across imaging modalities, build complex-valued datasets, and compare Plug-and-Play, diffusion and flow-matching paradigms against magnitude/phase splitting.

projects.title: A Cross-Cultural Study of Podcasts for Well-Being Information Dissemination
projects.summary: Examines how health and well-being topics are framed in podcasts across cultural and language contexts, combining NLP analysis of podcast metadata and transcripts with grounded theory, and relating framing choices to audience engagement.

projects.title: Adapting foundation models for knowledge transfer in out-of-distribution medical data
projects.summary: Develops adaptive fine-tuning methods for foundation models that reduce performance disparities under distribution shift in medical data, along with benchmarks and evaluation protocols for drift detection and equity-performance trade-offs.

projects.title: Advancing CT-Based Characterization of Poorly Understood Vascular Diseases Through Foundation Models
projects.summary: Aims to develop an interpretable computer-aided diagnostic tool for fibromuscular dysplasia in renal arteries from CTA scans, using segmentation of renal arteries and classification of lesions with machine learning, in collaboration with Idiap and CHUV.

projects.title: Agentic retrieval augmented generation interface for sleep Medicine
projects.summary: Focuses on building a Scientific Literature Agent using retrieval-augmented generation over sleep scoring guidelines and medical literature, integrating it with a central LLM and a GUI demonstrator for clinicians (OmniSleep project).

projects.title: An open-source framework for the quantification of Urban Heat Islands in Switzerland
projects.summary: Aims to build an open-source Python or C++ framework that converts Swiss open datasets into inputs for CitySim and ENVI-met, introduces Physiological Equivalent Temperature in CitySim, and quantifies urban heat mitigation scenarios on two Swiss case studies.

projects.title: Assessing Lyrics-Based Item Profiles for Music Information Retrieval
projects.summary: Studies whether text-based item profiles built from lyrics and lyric-related resources give more task-relevant representations than direct lyric embeddings for MIR tasks such as genre classification, mood or tag prediction, and retrieval.

projects.title: Audiovisual person recognition
projects.summary: Aims to combine audio and visual biometric person identification systems, either by developing them separately and fusing their outputs or by building a single system taking both embeddings as input, building on Idiap's NIST SRE 2019 scripts.

projects.title: Automatic identification of flight information from speech
projects.summary: Aims to develop a unified model, for example adapting BERT, that maps speech directly to aviation call-signs, and compare it with independently trained speech recognition and concept-extraction modules.

projects.title: Automatic named entity recognition from speech
projects.summary: Aims to improve recognition of named entities directly from speech by training the speech recognition and named entity recognition modules together end-to-end, and comparing this with independently trained modules.

projects.title: Automatic speech recognition of air-traffic communication using grammar
projects.summary: Aims to build a baseline ASR system for air-traffic controllers in Kaldi and to explore context-free grammar language modeling based on ICAO phraseology, either replacing or enriching statistical language models.

projects.title: Cognitive architecture for assistive robots
projects.summary: Aims to integrate the Lio robot with the DIARC cognitive architecture from Tufts HRILab, connecting it to ROS and developing human-robot interaction demos.

projects.title: Design of robotic teleoperation interface
projects.summary: Aims to design a web-based teleoperation interface for the Lio robot, covering navigation, manipulation, and speech, to support public demonstrations and assistive-robotics design studies with caregivers and users.

projects.title: Dynamic Frequency Allocation for Speech Separation
projects.summary: Investigates whether speech separation models such as TIGER should allocate frequency resolution dynamically per input mixture while keeping computational cost fixed. Includes analysis of per-utterance performance across fixed frequency partitions and a possible lightweight predictor of frequency allocation, with attention to pathological speech.

projects.title: Efficient Robot Data Collection through Geometric Shared Autonomy
projects.summary: Extends the GeoSACS interface, which represents task structure with a canal surface and lets users correct trajectories with a low-dimensional joystick, into a synchronized multimodal data-recording pipeline for robot manipulation. The project compares its data collection efficiency with conventional teleoperation and prepares datasets for imitation learning.

projects.title: Error correction in speech recognition using large pre-trained language models
projects.summary: Investigates whether large pre-trained language models can correct errors in speech transcription output, analysing error types and comparing traditional and conversational language models, including rescoring of N-best hypotheses.

projects.title: Faithful Vision-Language Explanations for Unified Face Attack Detection
projects.summary: Aims to build a face attack (presentation attack and deepfake) detector paired with a vision-language model that produces explanations, plus a verifier that tests whether generated claims are faithful by perturbing the claimed evidence. The work targets cross-dataset and unseen attack evaluation.

projects.title: From Audiobooks to Character Utterances: Automatic Annotation of Speakers in Literary Fiction
projects.summary: Aims to build a pipeline that automatically annotates speech utterances from LibriVox dramatic-reading audiobooks with their speaking character, to create a large annotated dataset for quotation attribution in fiction.

projects.title: From Gaze Following to Joint Attention
projects.summary: Trains and evaluates a transformer-based gaze following model on a new dataset, measuring gaze following and joint attention, then extends the architecture to predict joint attention end-to-end, in collaboration with the University of Zurich.

projects.title: From Personal Stories to Collective Narratives: Computational Analysis of Health Narratives in Podcasts
projects.summary: Aims to develop a computational framework that automatically identifies personal health narratives in podcast transcripts and clusters them to reveal recurring narrative themes.

projects.title: From Scientific Data to Citizen Communication: Weather Nowcasting in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea
projects.summary: Aims to build an end-to-end machine-learning pipeline for short-term torrential rain nowcasting in Malabo using open data, integrating a local weather station, and a basic text-based alert system tested in a real scenario, in collaboration with local partners.

projects.title: Gaze-Guided Shared Autonomy for Object Manipulation
projects.summary: Aims to add eye gaze as a source of user intent to a joystick-based shared autonomy framework for object manipulation, fusing gaze with joystick input to predict intent earlier and more accurately, especially in cluttered scenes.

projects.title: Multimodal Learning for Automated Grading of Retinal Inflammation in Dynamic Imaging
projects.summary: Aims to design and validate multimodal machine learning models that automatically detect and grade retinal inflammation from fluorescein angiography images and videos, and to identify interpretable imaging biomarkers.

projects.title: Parametric Gaze Following
projects.summary: Explores casting gaze following as prediction of a parametric probability distribution (e.g. mixture of Gaussians) instead of a heatmap, and proposes new metrics that capture more information about the predicted distribution.

projects.title: Pathological speech detection in adverse environments
projects.summary: Examines how state-of-the-art automatic speech processing approaches for diagnosing motor speech disorders perform under noise and reverberation typical of clinical recordings, and develops targeted approaches if relevant.

projects.title: Pathological speech enhancement
projects.summary: Examines the performance of state-of-the-art speech enhancement approaches on pathological speech (e.g. hearing loss, head and neck cancers, neurological disorders), and develops approaches targeting pathological speech if time permits.

projects.title: Person Head Detection
projects.summary: Aims to compile public head-annotated datasets and train and evaluate an object detector that localizes whole human heads, with data augmentation for extreme head poses, packaged as a reusable inference pipeline for gaze tracking and head pose estimation.

projects.title: Pseudo labeling of Sensitive Attributes in Medical Imaging for Demographically Fair Machine Learning
projects.summary: Develops machine learning models that pseudo-label sensitive attributes such as gender or age in medical imaging datasets lacking such annotations, and assesses the impact of these pseudo-labels on fairness and performance.

projects.title: Punctuation restoration on automatic speech recognition output
projects.summary: Aims to train a model that adds punctuation, and optionally capitalization, to ASR output to improve readability and usefulness for downstream tasks, evaluated on several languages and real scenarios.

projects.title: Research Spotlight: Crafting An Interactive Webpage Template for Showcasing Science
projects.summary: Aims to create a versatile, feature-rich webpage template for showcasing research papers, including interactive elements for model demonstrations, and to evaluate tools such as Streamlit and Gradio for this purpose.

projects.title: Robotics: Automated discovery of material properties using dextrous manipulation, vision tools, and learning agents.
projects.summary: Aims to develop a classification framework for solid and semi-solid materials in automated sampling workflows using the FR3 and UR3e robots, vision, and force-torque or rheological cues to identify properties such as viscosity, adhesiveness, cohesiveness and granularity.

projects.title: Scaling Pre-training for Gaze Following
projects.summary: Aims to pre-train gaze following models on large curated video datasets using pseudo-annotations from strong gaze following models, then fine-tune and evaluate them on annotated video datasets.

projects.title: Social media and crowdsourcing for social good
projects.summary: Offers several student projects within a multidisciplinary initiative on social media analytics, visualization of social and crowdsourced data, and smartphone apps for mobile crowdsourcing, with collaborators in Europe and the Majority World.

projects.title: Spatio-temporal Modeling of Human Behavior in Videos
projects.summary: Explores spatio-temporal video encoders trained end-to-end to extract features for facial behavior tasks such as head gesture and facial expression recognition, with possible weakly-supervised joint learning from pseudo-annotations.

projects.title: Speaker identification enhanced by the social network analyser
projects.summary: Aims to build a speaker identification baseline and a graph/network analysis tool, then combine speech and network information to improve person identification on simulated lawful-investigation data, using open-source tools such as SpeechBrain and SocNetV.

projects.title: Speech/Music Classification
projects.summary: Aims to develop a classifier that discriminates speech from music and possibly noise, starting from an evaluation of existing speech/music and voice activity detection approaches on established data.

projects.title: Towards Scalable and Interpretable Foundation Models for physiologicals signals recorded during human sleep
projects.summary: Aims to develop self-supervised pretraining strategies for polysomnographic and EEG signals, then fine-tune and evaluate the encoders on sleep staging and seizure detection, including cross-dataset generalization.

projects.title: Understanding generalization in deep learning
projects.summary: Studies how the inductive biases of architectures and data properties explain generalization in deep learning, through experiments with various architectures and datasets, with theoretical or practical emphasis depending on the student.

projects.title: Understanding the robustness of machine learning models on underspecified tasks
projects.summary: Studies how in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance of deep learning models evolves during pre-training and fine-tuning, aiming to develop model selection strategies for robust models and produce results suitable for a scientific publication.

projects.title: Using large pretrained language models in speech recognition
projects.summary: Measures how large pretrained language models perform in ASR by scoring the outputs of a speech recognition model and combining the scores to refine transcriptions, comparing model sizes and families and the value of retraining the language model.

projects.title: Whole-Body Manipulation with Explicit Self-Balancing Control for Humanoid Robots
projects.summary: Aims to develop a whole-body control strategy for a humanoid robot (Unitree G1) that jointly treats balance and manipulation, accounting for the mass and inertia of arms and manipulated objects. Part of the work may be carried out on-site at S3C in Biel.

projects.title: Applications of Spectral/Conditional-Gradient Optimizers in FL, RL, and Reasoning
projects.summary: MS project exploring where spectral and conditional-gradient optimizers (SCION/MuON-style) bring benefits beyond supervised training, namely federated learning, reinforcement learning and LLM-based reasoning. Students benchmark these optimizers against conventional baselines in those settings.

projects.title: Emerging Optimizers for Large-Batch Training (SCION, MuON, Spectral Methods)
projects.summary: MS project investigating geometry-aware optimizers such as SCION, MuON, Stochastic Spectral Descent and Frank-Wolfe-based variants for stable large-batch training of deep networks. Students characterize their memory footprint, preconditioning, critical batch size and stability versus Adam/Lion/Shampoo, and evaluate them on large-batch pipelines (transformers, MoE).

projects.title: Online Adaptation and Dynamic Geometry in Modern Optimizers
projects.summary: MS project on online adaptation mechanisms for geometry-aware optimizers, such as dynamically adjusting preconditioners, spectral norms, constraint radii, learning rates and FW-LMO approximations during training. The goal is to design low-memory algorithms that adapt to curvature and distribution drift, tested on large-scale training setups.

projects.title: Rethinking Diffusion Modeling from the Ground Up: Building a Diffusion-LLM
projects.summary: Project rethinking diffusion modeling from first principles to build a diffusion-based LLM as part of the Swiss AI Initiative. Students explore new discrete/structured diffusion formulations, prototype diffusion-LLM architectures, and compare them with autoregressive transformers, with a theoretical direction (combinatorial optimization and submodularity) and a large-scale implementation direction.

projects.title: Risk-Aware Selective Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Language Modeling
projects.summary: The project extends the risk-aware selective language modeling framework (ESLM) to Mixture-of-Experts architectures by designing a risk-aware routing mechanism that routes inputs to experts based on confidence and risk estimates. The goal is more efficient training and inference with robustness to distribution shifts and adversarial inputs, evaluated against standard MoE routing strategies.

projects.title: 3D Sound Localization
projects.summary: Build a toolbox that simulates human auditory localization to objectively assess how hearing aid algorithms preserve or distort spatial cues, replacing costly listening tests. The project has three stages: building a hearing-loss-aware 3D localization toolbox, measuring the HRTF of a Kemar dummy head, and validating the toolbox with listening tests involving about 10 normal-hearing and 20 hearing-impaired participants.

projects.title: Auditory distance perception
projects.summary: Evaluate how hearing aids affect the auditory distance perception of hearing-impaired listeners. The project has two stages: building a listening test facility with a loudspeaker on a precise motorised rail, then running listening tests with about 10 normal-hearing and 20 hearing-impaired participants.

projects.title: Controlling the timbre of wind instruments with active control
projects.summary: Develop a scaled prototype of an active wind instrument: a cylindrical hollow duct with a ring of active electroacoustic absorbers that change the acoustic impedance and alter the timbre. The work covers COMSOL FEM simulations, design and control of the prototype, and acoustic assessment of the resonators and the whole instrument.

projects.title: Design of unprecedented sound sources: a dream come true with plasma loudspeakers?
projects.summary: The project aims to identify and, if possible, implement a purely omnidirectional corona discharge (plasma) loudspeaker configuration approximating an ideal pulsating sphere, and optionally extend the work to other canonical electroacoustic sources. The work involves COMSOL and/or analytical modelling for geometry optimisation, followed by prototype construction and anechoic testing.

projects.title: Development and characterization of an acoustic matched source
projects.summary: The project aims to develop and characterize an acoustic matched source, using active control of a closed-box electrodynamic loudspeaker to achieve impedance matching. It includes a literature review, numerical FDTD/Simulink modelling, experimental measurements at multiple harmonics, and an extension to a broadband matched source using a corona discharge actuator.

projects.title: Development of a Graphical User Interface for Electroacoustic Absorbers
projects.summary: The student reviews the literature on Electroacoustic Absorbers (EA), builds an analytical Matlab model, and implements direct impedance control on a prototype using a Speedgoat real-time target with Matlab/Simulink. The project ends with a stand-alone GUI that lets a non-expert set control parameters and assess an EA's acoustic performance in an impedance tube.

projects.title: Enhancing Protein Design Through Advanced Graph Neural Networks
projects.summary: The project focuses on protein sequence design, creating protein sequences that perform specific functions for applications such as drug development and bioengineering. It will use advanced Graph Neural Networks to improve protein sequence design methods.

projects.title: Exploration and improvement of a data-agnostic multimodal deep learning architecture relying on a novel fusion strategy
projects.summary: Explore, improve and propose alterations of a data-agnostic, perceiver-based multimodal deep learning architecture that integrates modalities sequentially. The work includes adapting layers for efficiency or performance, researching pre-training approaches, and evaluating data encoding tactics and hybrid fusion methods.

projects.title: Modeling translation elongation dynamics through Variational AutoEncoders
projects.summary: The project models ribosome profiling density profiles with Variational AutoEncoders to capture translation elongation dynamics. The student first evaluates VAE reconstruction in a single condition, then extends the decoder to take nutrient availability into account.

projects.title: Optimization of corona discharge loudspeakers
projects.summary: The project aims to identify and implement corona discharge loudspeaker configurations with better sound radiation efficiency, notably a useful band-pass behaviour over a wide audible band. It will build a COMSOL and/or analytical model of the transducer for geometry optimization, then build and test prototypes in anechoic conditions.

projects.title: Plasmacoustic headphones
projects.summary: Simulate and implement a fully open corona-discharge (CD) headphone, optimizing the transducer geometry with a COMSOL and/or analytical model, then building prototypes and testing them on an artificial ear in anechoic conditions. The goal is to avoid the occlusion effect of conventional headphones while managing sound leakage to the environment.

projects.title: VENOVA : an actively modified cylindrical cross-saxophone
projects.summary: The project aims to design an actuator and couplings (CAD and 3D printing) added to the VENOVA instrument, then model how impedance control at the actuator can alter its sound, and implement, measure and playtest control strategies. Some experience with reed instruments is preferable but not required.

projects.title: Concept-based representations in pretrained vision models: concept bottleneck models vs sparse autoencoders
projects.summary: Compares concept bottleneck models (CBMs), sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and hybrids of the two for learning concept-oriented representations in pretrained vision models. The goal is to assess interpretability, disentanglement, information leakage, and downstream usefulness.

projects.title: Graph diffusion with joint node-edge constraints
projects.summary: Aims to develop a graph diffusion method that natively enforces joint node-edge constraints during generation, such as valence consistency in molecular graphs. The goal is to improve state-of-the-art performance on real-world tasks such as molecular design.

projects.title: Graph Latent Diffusion Models
projects.summary: Aims to develop a graph-specific latent diffusion model that runs the diffusion process in a lower-dimensional latent space, to scale graph generation beyond small graphs.

projects.title: Learning from Art Brut: reading cognitive signatures in artworks
projects.summary: Applies deep learning and computer vision to digitised Art Brut collections from Lausanne, Bern and Heidelberg to extract and cluster recurrent visual patterns across diagnoses and artists. The aim is to find cognitive signatures of mental disorders, in collaboration with art-history and symbolism experts.

projects.title: Low-rank edge representations for scalable graph transformers
projects.summary: Investigates low-rank edge representations in graph transformers used for graph diffusion, to reduce the memory cost of the dense edge state. The project quantifies expressivity of low-rank edges and tests an implementation on benchmarks, including large graphs.

projects.title: Machine learning for molecular identification from tandem mass spectra
projects.summary: Aims to identify small molecules from tandem mass spectrometry data, which mostly remain unmatched to structures. Possible directions include conditional graph generative models, self-supervised foundation models for spectra, combinatorial optimization over molecular space, and uncertainty quantification. The project has a strong research focus and may lead to a publication.

projects.title: Mechanistic interpretability of looped diffusion language models
projects.summary: Studies and compares the internal dynamics of standard masked diffusion language models and looped/recursive variants using lens-based interpretability tools such as Logit Lens, Tuned Lens and Jacobian Lens. The goal is to understand how and when predictions form across layers, loops and denoising steps.

projects.title: Neural ODE graph networks for latent graph trajectories
projects.summary: Uses a Neural ODE formulation to learn latent graph trajectories with graph neural networks for temporal data, separating spatial and temporal updates. The goal is interpretability of the flow field and learning in scarce-data settings.

projects.title: Optimal-transport-based train/test splits for distribution shift
projects.summary: Develops optimization-based methods that build challenging train/test splits by maximizing the optimal transport discrepancy between training and test sets. The project has five difficulty levels, scaled to bachelor, master short-project, or master thesis scope, and requires efficient algorithms for large datasets.

projects.title: Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for High-Resolution Mesh-Based Simulations
projects.summary: Explores physics-informed graph neural networks to scale mesh-based simulations to high resolution, using coarser surrogate representations and hierarchical multi-scale modeling. The initial testbed is wind-tunnel dynamics.

projects.title: Robust Automatic Pathological Speech Detection
projects.summary: Develops robust deep learning approaches for automatic pathological speech detection that withstand recording artifacts and spurious correlations such as noise disparity between classes. The aim is to support clinical assessment of speech disorders.

projects.title: Scalable Graph Generation via Link Prediction
projects.summary: Aims to make graph generation scalable by replacing quadratic-cost sparse graph transformers with message-passing and link prediction modules that match transformer performance. Goals include reproducing SparseDiff and exploring other scalable methods such as latent diffusion.

projects.title: Topoformer: A Spatial-Informed Foundation Model for Spatial-Biology
projects.summary: Builds a foundation model for spatial biology by converting tissue images into compact spatial tokens using topological data analysis, then training transformers with self-supervised pretraining on large public cohorts. Target tasks include patient stratification, survival prediction and biomarker discovery.

projects.title: Data-driven wave propagation modeling for ultrasound imaging
projects.summary: Investigate data-driven modeling strategies that build a proxy for the wave propagation operator directly from recorded ultrasound signals, avoiding full-wave simulations. The goal is a low-dimensional, cheap model compared against model-based wavefields across media of varying complexity.

projects.title: Deep Neural Network uncertainty quantification: beyond Deep Ensemble
projects.summary: Survey whether the reconstruction quality and uncertainty estimates of a deep ensemble can be obtained at lower cost with a single network or modified architecture. Compare input perturbation, weight perturbation (e.g. Laplace-style approximation), and Bayesian neural network architectures.

projects.title: Development of a pre-processing pipeline for diffusion-weighted MRI data followed by the implementation of a deep-learning-based automatic lymph-node segmentation tool
projects.summary: Build a body DW-MRI pre-processing pipeline with quality control and non-rigid co-registration, then design and evaluate a deep-learning model that automatically segments lymph nodes from the co-registered volumes. The work also compares supervised, transfer-learning and self/unsupervised data strategies.

projects.title: Physics-Informed Learning for Sparse Measurement Selection in Diffusion MRI Protocol Design
projects.summary: Use machine learning to select a compact subset of diffusion MRI measurements that remains informative for estimating white matter model parameters, guided by physics-informed criteria such as Fisher information. The learned protocol is to be compared with baseline selection strategies using simulations and parameter estimation.

projects.title: Project at CHUV – Mapping functional connectivity in callosal dysgenesis
projects.summary: Analyse ADC-fMRI data from a cohort of children with callosal dysgenesis, from diffusion MRI timeseries preprocessing to group comparisons of brain activity and functional connectivity. The project is based at the CHUV Radiology Research Unit with a start date of Fall 2026.

projects.title: Synthetic Stroke Lesion Simulation and Deep Learning Segmentation Using HCP Data
projects.summary: Develop a simulation framework that generates synthetic acute stroke lesions on high-quality HCP diffusion and structural MRI, then train a deep segmentation network on this synthetic data. The trained model is to be evaluated on real stroke images from open clinical datasets such as ISLES and on CHUV network prototypes.

projects.title: Wavefield Extrapolation in Polar Coordinates for Ultrasound Imaging in Heterogeneous Media
projects.summary: Derive and implement a paraxial approximation of the 2D Helmholtz equation in polar coordinates to extrapolate acoustic wavefields over smoothly varying sound-speed media for curved ultrasound arrays. The solver is to be validated on simulated ultrasound data and benchmarked for accuracy, stability and efficiency, and released as open-source code.

projects.title: Alignment-based conformance checking
projects.summary: Build a neuro-symbolic conformance checking framework that translates natural language regulatory articles (e.g. EU AI Act, GDPR) into linear temporal logic specifications and evaluates them on execution traces of multi-agent systems. The aim is a transparent mechanism that detects and explains compliance risks.

projects.title: Continuous latent flow matching for multimodal spatial reasoning
projects.summary: Develop a single-step continuous latent flow architecture that maps directly from multimodal inputs (video, audio, language instructions) to latent action-reasoning representations for Vision-Language-Action models. The aim is accurate spatial problem-solving in a single forward pass, replacing multi-step chain-of-thought generation.

projects.title: Contrastive latent alignment for multimodal reasoning
projects.summary: Explore a contrastive latent alignment process that enforces cross-modal and preference alignment within continuous latent reasoning paths, to handle conflicting sensory inputs that corrupt latent representations. Suggested methods include cross-modal contrastive trajectory optimization and direct preference alignment over continuous latent manifolds.

projects.title: Linguistic and stylometric style transfer for long-form speech anonymization
projects.summary: Use sequence-to-sequence style-transfer models to translate or obfuscate individual speaking styles, syntax and dialectal markers in long-form recordings, so speakers cannot be re-identified from linguistic cues. The focus is French/Italian or German, including Swiss German, with evaluation with human participants and real-world datasets in collaboration with RTS.

projects.title: Locating and ablating circuit-level private attribute sub-networks
projects.summary: Use activation-space dictionary learning to map the circuits that encode specific private attributes (PII) in AI models, then ablate or orthogonalize these latent directions. The goal is to remove PII while preserving zero-shot task performance, without retraining or fine-tuning the model.

projects.title: Privacy guarantees for speech anonymization
projects.summary: Build a framework that explicitly bounds and minimizes mutual information across speech modalities (acoustic, emotional prosody, linguistic stylometrics), providing information-theoretic privacy guarantees against adaptive adversaries. The work combines AI signal processing, deep generative modeling and privacy theory, with evaluation with human participants and RTS data.

projects.title: Visual stream parsing for compliance auditing
projects.summary: Design a dynamic legal-visual (or legal-audio-visual) concept engine that extends static concept probing to real-time video streams. It would fuse vision-language or audio-visual-language streaming backbones with ontology graph mapping to track entities, infer sensitive personal attributes and map scene semantics to legal frameworks.

projects.title: Voice anonymization with preservation of emotional prosody in multilingual settings
projects.summary: Design, implement and evaluate an AI-based acoustic transformation framework that masks speaker identity while preserving emotional prosody, semantic meaning and intelligibility. The focus is French/Italian or German, including Swiss German, with evaluation with human participants and real-world datasets in collaboration with RTS.

projects.title: Biophysical Modelling of Microstructural Diffusion MRI in the Rodent Brain
projects.summary: Uses advanced biophysical models of diffusion MRI to extract quantitative maps of brain microstructure in animal models of disease compared with healthy controls. Possible applications mentioned include Parkinson's disease and creatine-related conditions.

projects.title: Community Detection in Directed (Brain) Networks
projects.summary: Aims to develop community detection for directed and asymmetric networks, such as brain networks, rather than symmetric graphs.

projects.title: Developmental Trajectories of Perinatal Resting-State fMRI dynamics
projects.summary: Investigates the maturation of brain functional dynamics during the perinatal period, for example by applying Co-Activation Pattern (CAP) analysis.

projects.title: Dynamic mode decomposition of fMRI during film watching
projects.summary: Applies dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), a latent space discovery method, to fMRI data acquired during naturalistic film watching.

projects.title: Encoding and Decoding fMRI during film watching
projects.summary: Studies human brain decoding and encoding during naturalistic stimuli, namely film watching, extending prior work on simple images.

projects.title: Graph signal processing to investigate structure-function coupling during sleep
projects.summary: Treats fMRI signals as defined on the structural brain graph to study how functional activity emerges from anatomical fiber bundles during sleep, using graph signal processing.

projects.title: Investigating memory consolidation during sleep with functional MRI
projects.summary: Uses a dataset of lucid dreamers scanned with fMRI during a hand motor sequence training, both awake and during sleep, to study memory consolidation mechanisms.

projects.title: Longitudinal Brain Connectomics and Functional Fingerprinting in Chronic Tinnitus
projects.summary: A semester or MSc thesis project investigating how large-scale brain networks reorganize during neurofeedback treatment for chronic tinnitus.

projects.title: Structural connectivity of the human brain: what can we learn from intracerebral electrophysiological recordings in epileptic patients?
projects.summary: Explores how intracerebral electrophysiological recordings in epileptic patients can inform the structural connectivity of the human brain, using a connectomics framework for healthy and pathological brain data.

projects.title: The role of the hippocampus in tracking personal goals
projects.summary: Analyses fMRI scans of healthy subjects performing specific goal-directed tasks to study the role of the hippocampus in distinguishing goals over time.

projects.title: Unraveling the contrast mechanism of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI
projects.summary: Aims to understand the contrast mechanism of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI, a technique that detects pathological alterations in diseases such as Parkinson's disease and schizophrenia. The technique is thought to reflect catecholaminergic function rather than directly measuring neuromelanin.

projects.title: Deep learning for deepfake detection
projects.summary: Train convolutional neural networks in a supervised way to detect deepfake images and videos, collecting existing deepfake datasets and studying ensembles of trained CNNs. The student assesses performance across several datasets.

projects.title: Image compression for DNA based storage
projects.summary: Study state-of-the-art approaches for storing information in DNA and build an end-to-end image compression simulator for DNA storage based on publicly available implementations. The student analyses the simulator's performance.

projects.title: Mobile App for Privacy Protection on iOS or Android Platform
projects.summary: Develop a smartphone app that obfuscates personal visual information in images in a secure and recoverable way, with multi-region selection by touch and a simple key management system. The app should also support sharing protected images on social networks.

projects.title: Representation and interpretation of a Factuality Trust Indicator in JPEG Trust
projects.summary: Define and implement a JPEG Trust compatible way to represent content-based factuality information in media assets, with tools to generate and read it. The student builds Trust Profile examples combining factuality with other trust information and evaluates how factuality affects the Trust Report.

projects.title: Reverse image search for media-context verification in multimodal fact-checking
projects.summary: Build a component that searches the Web for earlier appearances of a submitted image and recovers their date, location and event, to improve detection of out-of-context misinformation in a JPEG Trust fact-checking pipeline. The work includes comparing candidate tools and evaluating on multimodal misinformation datasets.

projects.title: Algorithmic collusion in electricity markets
projects.summary: Semester project investigating collusive outcomes when autonomous agents learn to bid in electricity markets, mainly through numerical simulations combined with theory.

projects.title: Controlling a Multi-drone Fleet for Traffic Monitoring
projects.summary: Coordinate a fleet of UAVs that collect traffic data at multiple locations, deciding where and when each drone collects data based on road importance and previous visits.

projects.title: Hybrid soft-actor critic benchmark
projects.summary: Benchmark a hybrid variant of soft actor-critic (SAC) that learns to autonomously build an arch, a task with a mix of continuous and discrete actions, against existing methods such as hybrid PPO.

projects.title: Multi-Agent Traffic Monitoring with Limited Information Sharing
projects.summary: Coordinate a UAV fleet that collects traffic data where fixed sensors are absent, prioritising important roads under limited information sharing between drones.

projects.title: Multi-Objective Optimization for Automated Theorem Proving
projects.summary: Work on automated theorem proving, where large language models trained with reinforcement learning generate formal proofs checked by proof assistants such as Lean or Isabelle.

projects.title: Reinforcement learning to achieve efficient equilibria in repeated games with partial observability
projects.summary: Design online learning algorithms that learn efficient equilibria of a long-horizon repeated game, focusing on leader-follower games where the follower's actions are partially observable. Master's thesis project at the intersection of reinforcement learning and game theory.

projects.title: Algorithms robust to errors in 3T-1C GC-eDRAM
projects.summary: Explore algorithms that can tolerate the random data losses of gain-cell eDRAM (GC-eDRAM) caused by limited retention time, such as neural networks and error-correction codes. The goal is to build a model relating algorithm accuracy to system power.

projects.title: Analog High-Performance Sorters for Telecommunications
projects.summary: Evaluate mixed-signal architectures for sorters that find the U smallest elements in large sets, as needed in 5G/6G and high-speed fiber systems. Optimize area, power and speed and compare against purely digital implementations in 16nm FinFET.

projects.title: Cellular Sensing: Traffic Safety Alert
projects.summary: Use real-time channel state information from cellular signals to detect the speed of approaching vehicles and classify traffic as safe or dangerous, to alert distracted pedestrians.

projects.title: Characterization of an in-memory computing on Silicon
projects.summary: Characterize two fabricated 65nm BLADE in-memory computing configurations across voltage and temperature conditions, using on-board test programs to extract memory metrics and verify functionality.

projects.title: Chip for Wi-Fi sensing
projects.summary: Move the lab's current FPGA-based Wi-Fi sensing system (activity detection, localization, vital-sign estimation) to a semi-custom ASIC, optimizing for area, power and speed. Work involves circuit design in Cadence with a standard-cell flow, plus exploration with VHDL/Verilog.

projects.title: chip2chip serial-link for RISC-V Microcontrollers
projects.summary: Integrate a chip-to-chip serial-link IP into X-HEEP so two microcontrollers can exchange memory-mapped read/write data, extending the Pynq-Z2 FPGA support and testing on two FPGAs.

projects.title: Compact low-static-power CAM bitcell
projects.summary: Design and simulate a novel compact CAM (content-addressable memory) bitcell with lower static leakage than conventional compact (<6T) cells, while keeping fast match-line evaluation. The design is to be validated under PVT variations and mismatch. Suited to 1-2 students.

projects.title: Configurable NM-Caesar near-memory computing RTL
projects.summary: Improve the NM-Caesar near-memory computing RTL so that memory size and number of banks are configurable. The work also aims to optimize the design and highlight energy, area and performance trade-offs.

projects.title: Decoder with Bit-Flipping Post-Processing for 6G wireless
projects.summary: Develop a low-complexity bit-flipping post-processing decoder for 6G wireless, design its hardware architecture, implement it in VHDL, and benchmark and optimize it.

projects.title: Design automation of in-memory computing
projects.summary: Automate the physical design of the BLADE in-memory computing architecture for arbitrary configurations in 65nm, starting with the memory decoder and local memory controller, and later explore open-source PnR tools.

projects.title: Design of A Matrix with Multiple Sizes and Its Decoder Implementation
projects.summary: Given a base matrix, design LDPC matrices with several lifting sizes (smaller ones nested in larger ones), analyze them in Matlab or C++, and verify them in a configurable LDPC ASIC decoder.

projects.title: Design of a Wireless Modem for IoT
projects.summary: Implement a LoRa transmitter: build a golden model including fixed-point arithmetic, design and implement its architecture in VHDL with a bus interface, and test it on an FPGA.

projects.title: Designing a decoder in 16nm FinFet
projects.summary: Implement a full-custom GRAND-based error-correction decoder in 16nm FinFET using dynamic logic and an in-memory computation style, and automate layout generation with Python scripts.

projects.title: Designing a Leakage Suppression SRAM / ROM in 16nm FinFET
projects.summary: Evaluate leakage suppression techniques on a memory macro for an always-on low-power circuit, characterize speed and leakage, and design a bitcell array with leakage suppression.

projects.title: Designing Analog Blocks for the GC-eDRAM at 16nm FINFET
projects.summary: Design well-known analog blocks (ADC and voltage buffers) for characterizing the new GC-eDRAM macro in 16nm FinFET technology, including literature research, layout and post-layout optimization.

projects.title: DPTLSL leakage-suppression logic characterization
projects.summary: Characterize and optimize cells and circuit architecture for the DPTLSL leakage-suppression logic family developed at TCL, targeting low-leakage, reliable operation for a FIR filter circuit. The work includes comparison with a standard CMOS library.

projects.title: DPTLSL RISC-V System-On-Chip
projects.summary: Build a very small version of the X-HEEP RISC-V microcontroller (CPU, one memory bank, GPIOs) and synthesize it with a custom differential-logic standard-cell library, producing a verified post-synthesis netlist.

projects.title: Drone Detection Radar Design
projects.summary: Design an RF circuit on PCB to detect the speed and position of drones, model the RF system for simulation, and process the data on a software-defined radio for real-time signal processing.

projects.title: Efficient MVM for Syndrome Computation in Decoders
projects.summary: Design a full-custom GF(2) matrix-vector multiplication accelerator in 16nm FinFET for syndrome computation in channel decoders, and compare it with standard-cell implementations in efficiency and performance.

projects.title: Elaboration of an In-Memory Computing Memory Compiler (Master Thesis)
projects.summary: Design an in-memory computing memory compiler in 65nm using open-source tools that generates GDS, LEF, LIB and SPICE files from memory size and configuration. Work covers physical design, simulation, characterization and scripting automation.

projects.title: Experimental evaluation of an SDR LoRa implementation
projects.summary: Evaluate the error-rate performance of the group's open-source software-defined radio (SDR) implementation of LoRa and compare it with commercial LoRa hardware implementations, using experimental evaluation with SDRs.

projects.title: GC-RAM Controller for X-HEEP
projects.summary: Design and implement a smart memory controller for dynamic GC-RAM integrated into the X-HEEP platform, handling refresh, access multiplexing, error detection and correction, and interfacing to a system bus.

projects.title: High-Throughput Hard-Decision Decoder for Optical Communications
projects.summary: Develop a low-complexity iterative bounded-distance hard-decision decoder for two-dimensional parity codes targeting 400G-800G optical fiber standards, implement it in VHDL, and benchmark it.

projects.title: Improved Belief Propagation Decoding for Short Codes
projects.summary: Improve sparse parity-check matrix transformations for belief propagation decoding of short codes, using machine learning, and construct short linear codes suited to sparse BP decoding for 6G uRLLC. Recommended for groups of at least two students.

projects.title: Improving blocks of the GC-eDRAM in 28nm FDSOI Process
projects.summary: Design new full-custom analog blocks (charge pump, sense amplifier) for the GC-eDRAM macro in 28nm FDSOI to extend data retention time, including simulation, layout and post-layout optimization.

projects.title: Integrating High-Speed Test Infrastructure into XHeep (Semester Project)
projects.summary: Integrate the IPbus-based high-speed Ethernet test infrastructure, already used at TCL for testing custom ASICs, into the XHeep project to replace slow legacy test interfaces.

projects.title: Interconnect-aware BP decoder architecture study (routing congestion)
projects.summary: Compare routing behavior of different belief-propagation (BP) decoder architectures to identify interconnect bottlenecks and scaling limits. The goal is to derive guidelines for a scalable, interconnect-aware BP decoder, evaluating how wire congestion affects area, power and delay.

projects.title: Low-complexity FEC decoding for optical communication
projects.summary: Explore forward error correction (FEC) decoding algorithms that meet optical communication standards for AI data center networks, and reduce their decoding complexity. Hardware decoder implementation is optional.

projects.title: Machine-learning-based drone localization with LoRa
projects.summary: Implement machine learning models that estimate drone location from noisy LoRa RSSI/SNR signals, using about 75k drone measurements taken around EPFL with four campus gateways. The goal is to evaluate their performance and robustness in LoRa-based IoT systems.

projects.title: Mioty Implementation
projects.summary: Improve the synchronization of an existing open-source software-defined radio implementation of the Mioty LPWAN standard so it works in real-world communications, and build a transceiver compatible with commercial devices.

projects.title: Mixed signal compute block
projects.summary: Design analog sorter blocks, including DACs and comparators, compatible with standard-cell dimensions, as a mixed-signal approach to accelerate digital bottlenecks in 5G/6G algorithms.

projects.title: Morphological filter circuit architectures (iterative, pipelined, unrolled)
projects.summary: Starting from a Python description of morphological filters (erosion, dilation, opening, closing), design three hardware circuit architectures (iterative, pipelined, unrolled). Compare them through post-synthesis power, performance and area (PPA) extraction.

projects.title: Multi-Bit Error Correction Code (ECC) for Gain-Cell eDRAM
projects.summary: Explore a better trade-off between parity storage overhead, latency and system power for multi-bit error correction in gain-cell eDRAM, then design, verify and implement the chosen ECC in ASIC.

projects.title: Open Reimplementation of the RP2040 PIO (Master Thesis)
projects.summary: Read the specifications of the Raspberry Pi RP2040 programmable I/O (PIO) block, implement its state machines in RTL, and integrate the result into the HEEP system with FPGA prototyping.

projects.title: Optimize Gain-Cell eDRAM Performance on X-Heep Platform
projects.summary: Optimize the cache line structure of gain-cell eDRAM on the X-Heep SoC platform by adding one or more buffer cache lines, to reduce read-modify-write and refresh overhead. Requires running benchmarks and hardware/software co-optimization.

projects.title: Project 1: Localization and User Activity Detection
projects.summary: Collect and label Wi-Fi signal data for different activities and locations, develop preprocessing and classification or localization models, and present a system detecting user activity, room state and location.

projects.title: Project 1: LoRa Transceiver Optimization and Evaluation
projects.summary: Characterize the open-source LoRa transceiver in terms of memory footprint, computational load and performance, then add features to the public repository.

projects.title: Project 2: LoRaWAN for SDR
projects.summary: Add LoRaWAN support to the open-source LoRa transceiver by creating an interface between an existing MAC-layer library and the SDR implementation in GNU Radio.

projects.title: Project 2: Vital-Signs Estimation
projects.summary: Use reflected wireless signals to estimate breathing rates of one or several people in different scenarios, collecting data and developing preprocessing and estimation models.

projects.title: Project 3: Hardware and Machine Learning for Enhancing Wi-Fi Radar
projects.summary: Design, implement and test a quantized neural-network canceller that removes the router's own transmit signal from received Wi-Fi signals, so that environmental reflections can be sensed.

projects.title: Project 3: Implementing a Mioty Transceiver
projects.summary: Build the first open-source software-defined radio implementation of a simple Mioty LPWAN transceiver and verify its compatibility with commercial radio chips.

projects.title: Project 4: 4G LTE Localization
projects.summary: Adapt an open-source 4G software radio suite to collect channel state information from LTE signals and use it to localize devices or device-free targets.

projects.title: Project 4: Characterizing the New WiFi HaLow
projects.summary: Set up a WiFi HaLow test environment at EPFL, define a test plan, and measure the performance and power of the first WiFi HaLow network in Switzerland, then write a report.

projects.title: Project 5: UWB Environment and Human Activity Sensing
projects.summary: Sense environments, vital signs and human activities from UWB/Wi-Fi channel estimates by synchronizing and preprocessing channel impulse responses and extracting activity information.

projects.title: Routing Design for Data Coupling in Decoders
projects.summary: Simplify the design of a flexible routing network that supports global coupling between cores in a multi-core LDPC decoder, analyze its performance in Matlab or C++, and implement it in ASIC.

projects.title: Test of the fabricated GC-eDRAM chip
projects.summary: Characterize fabricated GC-eDRAM chips in the lab by establishing communication with the chip, measuring temperature, voltage and frequency behavior, and comparing results with CAD simulations.

projects.title: Test Platform of Error-Correction Decoders on FPGA SoC
projects.summary: Build a reconfigurable FPGA SoC test platform for error-correction decoders (5G, 6G, optical), configuring I/O and CPU-FPGA communication, implementing and benchmarking the platform.

projects.title: Ultra-low power standard-cells library optimization for AO systems
projects.summary: Optimize, design and characterize a full-custom differential standard-cell library (DPTLSL) for always-on, leakage-dominated systems, and compare it with a standard CMOS library.

projects.title: 3D density map embedding for cryoEM
projects.summary: Build density map embeddings that capture the information in the cryoEM voxel grid using an autoencoder, and evaluate their biological meaningfulness. The project is a collaboration between the Laboratory for Biomolecular Modeling and the Computer Vision Laboratory.

projects.title: Behavioral studies in the laboratory
projects.summary: Hands-on experimental work with flies to examine how neural activation or other perturbations modulate animal behavior. The student designs experiments and analyzes their own data.

projects.title: Build a robotic fly
projects.summary: Construct an insect-inspired robot and test bioinspired algorithms of limb control, in collaboration with EPFL robotics groups. Nature's solutions to autonomous behavioral control are to be leveraged in robotics.

projects.title: Build artificial neural networks to control a simulated fly.
projects.summary: Develop biorealistic controllers for a physics-based neuromechanical simulation of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster. The project lies at the interface of robotics, computer science and neuroscience, possibly in collaboration with the BioRobotics Laboratory.

projects.title: Study the full graph (connectome) of the fly nervous system
projects.summary: Improve and explore the fly connectome graph to answer specific questions about neural circuit motifs underlying complex motor behaviors. The project sits at the interface of computer science, mathematics and biology.

projects.title: Use computational tools to study animal behavior
projects.summary: Use computational and machine learning approaches to quantify and segment fly behaviors into individual actions, and link these behavioral sequences to simultaneously acquired neuroimaging data.

projects.title: Use computational tools to study neural circuit activity
projects.summary: Use computer vision and machine learning to extract neural activity patterns during behavior and make predictions linking behavioral and internal states. The project sits at the interface of computer science and neurobiology.

projects.title: Use robotic systems to automate biological experimentation
projects.summary: Develop automated vision-guided robotic systems that perform behavioral and/or neural experiments, to automate and democratize biological experimentation. The project sits at the interface of robotics and neurobiology, possibly in collaboration with the Microrobotics Laboratory.

projects.title: Masters project: AI-based generative approaches for de novo protein design
projects.summary: Develop diffusion generative deep-learning models to design de novo proteins with precise functions for biomedical applications. The student would help integrate physics-based loss functions into the lab's existing deep learning framework.

projects.title: A Cross-Species Meta-Analysis of Astrocyte Transcriptional Diversity in Development and Disease (Dry)
projects.summary: Computational meta-analysis integrating public mouse and human single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq and multiomics datasets to build a cross-species astrocyte transcriptomic atlas. The project maps developmental and disease-associated astrocyte states and links them to GWAS risk loci for neurological and psychiatric disorders.

projects.title: Ex utero metabolic perturbation of the developing mouse brain
projects.summary: Wet and dry lab project in which the student acutely perturbs lipid metabolism in ex utero cultured mouse embryos during early brain formation. Effects are assessed with MALDI imaging mass spectrometry, spatial transcriptomics and confocal microscopy, followed by computational integration of spatial datasets.

projects.title: Linking Neuronal Function to Molecular Identity in Mouse Barrel Cortex (Dry and Wet)
projects.summary: Interdisciplinary project combining in vivo two-photon calcium imaging with spatial transcriptomics (Direct HybISS) to relate the activity of neurons to their molecular identity in adult mouse barrel cortex. The student contributes to an experimental pipeline that registers the same neurons across functional imaging and post-mortem transcriptomics.

projects.title: Circadian clocks in disease states and cancer
projects.summary: A semester project studying circadian clocks in disease states and cancer.

projects.title: Deep Learning Analysis of Human Histology Images
projects.summary: A semester project applying deep learning to analyse human histology images, as listed under the available semester projects.

projects.title: Latent space models for cyclic biomolecular processes and application to live microscopy imaging
projects.summary: A semester project developing latent space models for cyclic biomolecular processes, with application to live microscopy imaging.

projects.title: Machine learning multiomics data to identify gene regulatory networks across time, sex and tissues
projects.summary: A semester project using machine learning on multiomics data to identify gene regulatory networks across time, sex and tissues.
